audits.summary:
Audit of src/render/xray/heart.ts, coronaryTree.ts and thorax.ts (plus the projection and scene code they depend on). I compared them with the CC0/CC BY cine library and with literature I opened, mostly PubMed abstracts and the full text of Medrano-Gracia 2017 (DOIs in sources). All tools are in /private/tmp/claude-502/cathmaster-research/anatomy/: Node stdlib + sips image I/O, catheter calibration, minimal-path centreline tracing, NCC landmark tracking, tortuosity spectra and transect counts, and esbuild-bundled probes of the real simulator code. No project files were modified.

**What already matches.**
- Calibres agree with Dodge 1992 QCA values: LM 4.4–4.6 mm, proximal LAD 3.6 mm, proximal RCA 3.8 mm (right-dominant).
- LM length (10 mm) and the LM bifurcation angle (69°) fall inside CT-atlas ranges.
- At the ≥0.7 mm level, the number of branches crossing mid-tree transects is close to real (sim 5–6 versus real 4–8).

**Main findings, most important first.**

1. **Cranial and caudal are swapped.** `cameraBasis` sets n.y = −cosθ·sinφ and `makeCamera` puts the detector at +n. So "cranial" tilts the detector towards the feet; DICOM 0018,1511 defines +90 as cranial.
   - Projected checks and live renders (via the `__pciDraw` hook) agree. The "LAO CRA" preset renders a compact spider with no diaphragm. The "SPIDER" preset renders a long LAD running down the middle, which is what real LAO cranial runs look like.
   - This contradicts the app's own teaching text and plausibly explains the previously noted ~20 grey-level lighter LAO cranial calibration.
2. **Cardiac motion is wrong in several ways.**
   - Twist runs the wrong way (the apex turns clockwise seen from the apex) and totals only 8°. Normal values are apex counter-clockwise about 9–10° and base clockwise about 4–7°.
   - The aortic root, LM and catheter do not move with the beat. The proximal RCA moves 1.3 mm, whereas real proximal landmarks move 6–25 mm.
   - Real RCA versus LAD in-plane amplitude is 17.8 versus 8.2 mm (ratio 2.2); the simulator gives about 1.4. Real median speeds are 48 and 17 mm/s, against a 4.6 mm/s noise floor.
   - The simulator uses one phase-normalised contraction bump for every vessel. Its median frame-to-frame speed is 0–5 mm/s and the heart is still for about half the cycle. That still fraction grows with heart rate, whereas Husmann 2007 shows diastole shortens disproportionately.
3. **Vessels have almost no small-scale tortuosity.** RMS tangent-angle undulation in the 8–20 mm wavelength band is 6.5–22° (median about 11°) in real traces, against 1.2–2.1° in the simulator and 1.7–3.9° for the catheter-shaft noise floor. In the 3–8 mm band it is 9–19° real versus 0.2–0.9° simulated.
4. **The proximal geometry has kinks.** The heart frame's anterior AV groove sits above the LM ostium, so the Hermite bridge makes the LAD climb 14.5 mm above the bifurcation and the LCx 11 mm before descending. This produces Z-kinks at the LM and proximal RCA that are absent from real frames. The LM ostium is also placed higher than the RCA ostium, which is the opposite of Philip 2015.
5. **The heart shadow does not line up with the vessels and does not beat.**
   - Obtuse-margin vessels lie 8–12 mm inside the myocardial ellipsoid and 24–29 mm inside the lung-carving fat ellipsoid; the RCA lies up to 9 mm outside it.
   - `buildThorax` receives no contraction input, so vessels move over a static silhouette.
   - In a real frame, a marginal vessel runs within about 1 mm of the heart–lung border.
6. **There is no anatomical variability.**
   - Eight case seeds give LAD projected lengths of 156.2–157.1 mm.
   - Topology is fixed: 3 diagonals, 5 septals, 2 OMs, 1 RV branch and 1 AM, plus 22–24 parallel "twigs" per main vessel. There is no SA- or AV-nodal artery and no PDA septals.
   - Several variants are ignored: separate ostia (no LCx origin from `leftOstium2`), shepherd's crook and tortuous RCA. There is no myocardial bridging.
   - At each bifurcation the daughter diameters are too large for the parent. Cube ratios are 1.43–1.70; Finet ratios are 0.53–0.56 against 0.678, and Medrano-Gracia 2017 found the Huo–Kassab model the best fit.
7. **Breathing is too shallow and too simple.** Quiet breathing uses 7 mm of diaphragm excursion, below the 0.9–1.0 cm lower limit of normal (Boussuges), and is a pure translation. Shechter 2006 says breathing motion is more complex than a translation.
8. **The thorax is identical for every patient.** The pulmonary trees come from a fixed `prng(7)`, and there is no descending-aorta tube.

**Proposed upgrade, roughly in order.**
- Fix the projection sign, guarded by tests.
- Add a seeded `AnatomyGenome` sampled from sourced priors:
  - dominance 81/9/10 at autopsy, or 86.5/13.5 in the dataset's real-distribution subset;
  - ramus about 30%;
  - diagonals single/double/multiple 14/62/24% and marginals 20/51/29%;
  - wrap-around LAD 57–86%;
  - SA-nodal artery from the RCA 68% or LCx 22%;
  - myocardial bridging 6% at angiography, 82% on the LAD.
- Grow branches by territory-guided geodesics and space colonisation on one smooth biventricular `heartShape`. Size them with the Huo–Kassab 7/3 diameter law. Add a band-limited 3D tortuosity field calibrated to the measured spectra.
- Replace the motion with a time-based multi-phase `heartMotion` field: correct twist sign, base descent, whole-heart translation, root and catheter motion, regional lags, and a diastasis that shrinks with heart rate. Fit amplitudes to tracked library cines.
- Derive the renderer's analytic heart ellipsoids from the same deforming shape, so vessels sit on the silhouette and the silhouette beats.
- Longer term, build a CC0 library of real 3D coronary trees by multi-view triangulation of the CoronaryDominance runs, which carry positioner angles. Add a non-browser validation harness that checks these metrics against library ranges.

**Caveat on scale.** Millimetre values for real images assume the catheter is 6 F (0.31 mm/px); if 5 F, scale them by 0.83. Ratios do not depend on this.

gaps.gap: Cranial and caudal angulation are inverted in the camera basis used by the WebGL X-ray renderer (and the old cone-beam overlay), so every cranial preset renders as the corresponding caudal view and vice versa.
gaps.evidence: Code: src/simulation/projection.ts cameraBasis sets n.y = -cos(th)*sin(ph). makeCamera (sceneBuilder.ts) places the detector at iso + n*(SID-SOD), so cranialCaudal=+30 gives a detector direction with y = -0.50, i.e. towards the feet. DICOM (0018,1511) Positioner Secondary Angle defines +90 as cranial (dicom.innolitics.com, opened). Projected LAD length (AP, orthographic) is 125 mm at +30 versus 134 mm at -30; true cranial angulation elongates the LAD. Real library: LAO cranial runs (e.g. cdm-00893-LCA-4, LAO33 CRA27) show a long LAD down the middle with the diaphragm overlapping the heart. A sim projection at code +27 is a compact spider; at code -27 it matches the real image. Live app renders (PCI lab, __pciDraw(1.6), background tab): the 'SPIDER' preset (LAO 42/-28) shows a long vertical LAD; 'LAO CRA' and 'AP CRA' show compact radiating trees with no diaphragm. The app's own teaching text (src/content/tracks/foundations.ts:315) says a diaphragm overlying the heart indicates cranial tilt. The earlier calibration note that LAO cranial runs about 20 grey levels too light fits a missing diaphragm overlap.
gaps.proposal: Change n.y to +cos(th)*sin(ph) in cameraBasis and keep the right/up derivation, so one fix covers makeCamera and coneBeamCamera. Re-check every consumer: FluoroView 2D overlay, view trainer, PCI and diagnostic presets in src/data/viewPresets.ts, the AEC path-length formula in sceneBuilder. Add tests: (1) cranialCaudal>0 puts the detector at y>0; (2) AP cranial LAD projected length exceeds AP caudal; (3) the left diaphragm dome top projects higher relative to the heart centre in cranial than in caudal. Re-run the grey-level calibration against the CoronaryDominance percentiles afterwards.

gaps.gap: The motion field is physiologically wrong in sign, distribution and timing: twist is reversed and small; the aortic root, ostia, LM and catheter do not move with the beat; RCA motion is too small relative to LAD; and one phase-normalised bump is shared by every vessel, so the heart freezes for about half of each cycle.
gaps.evidence: Probe of heart.ts surfacePoint: apical rotation sign dot(L, r0×r1) = -39.9 (clockwise seen from the apex), basal +80.1 (counter-clockwise); twist = 8e(uM-0.4) totals 8°. Literature: apex counter-clockwise 10.2±4.8° and base clockwise 7.0±3.3° (Cheng 2017 CMR-FT); apex 9.2±3.2°, base -3.8±1.8°, twist 13.1±3.4° in controls (Halcsik 2026); base clockwise and apex counter-clockwise (Buckberg 2011). Sim ED-to-ES projected displacement: LM 0 mm (w=0); RCA at 10% 1.3 mm; RCA mid 10-11 mm (LAO); LAD mid 7-8 mm (RAO cranial); distal LAD 0.4-1.5 mm. Real tracking (NCC on vesselness, landmarks at 10/30/50/70/90% of traced centrelines, P10-P90 range over contrast frames, 6F scale): RCA LAO median 17.8 mm (IQR 11.1-23.2, 19 landmarks/4 runs); LAD RAO cranial 8.2 mm (5.8-11.7, 24/5); ratio 2.2 versus about 1.4 in the sim. Real proximal (10%) landmarks moved 6-25 mm; the LM/catheter-tip region in cdm-00931-LCA-1 moved about 27 px (≈8 mm) per beat. Real median frame-to-frame speed at 15 f/s: RCA 48 mm/s, LAD 17 mm/s (static-landmark noise floor 4.6 mm/s). Achenbach 2000 EBCT mean velocities: RCA 69.5, LAD 22.4, LCx 48.4 mm/s. Sim median speed is 0-5 mm/s. contraction() rises at phase 0.09-0.38 and returns by 0.55; the still fraction at 15 f/s is 0.53/0.56/0.60 at 60/72/90 bpm (rises with HR), whereas Husmann 2007 shows HR shortens systole and diastole nonproportionally. Shechter 2006 (abstract): arteries move left, inferior and anterior during contraction, with larger RCA displacement.
gaps.proposal: New src/render/xray/heartMotion.ts holding a time-based (ms) waveform: isovolumic contraction, ejection (near-constant duration), isovolumic relaxation, rapid filling with fast return, diastasis that shrinks with HR, and atrial kick as a small second excursion. Define a material-point displacement field u(ell,phi,h,t) as the sum of: longitudinal base descent fading to the apex; twist with the correct sign (apex counter-clockwise about 9°, base clockwise about 4°, scaled by contractility); radial thickening; whole-heart translation towards left-inferior-anterior; and an annulus/root motion field. Apply that last field to w<1 samples and to the catheter's root segment, so the catheter tip bobs with the ostium and engagement.ts sees relative motion (deep seating, loss of engagement). Add per-region phase lags (RV/RCA ahead) and regional hypokinesis. Fit amplitudes and directions per segment to the library: run the trace+track pipeline on about 30 RCA LAO and 30 LCA RAO/AP cranial runs and minimise the projected P10-P90 error per segment.

gaps.gap: Coronary centrelines are smooth arcs: the only small-scale shape is a 1.2° (large vessels) to 2.6° azimuth wiggle with roughly 53 mm and 21 mm wavelengths. Real vessels carry sub-millimetre to millimetre undulations at 3-20 mm wavelengths (and corkscrew coiling in some patients).
gaps.evidence: Tangent-angle band RMS (1 mm resampling, difference-of-moving-averages bands) on minimal-path traces of real frames (6F scale) versus sim projections in the same views. 8-20 mm band: real LAD RAO cranial 15.5/7.7/11.2/7.9/22.4°; real RCA LAO 12.4/6.5/11.3/10.7°; sim LAD 2.0-2.1°, sim RCA 1.2-1.7°; catheter-shaft noise floor 1.7-3.9°. 3-8 mm band: real 9.0-18.6°; sim 0.2-0.9°; catheter floor 6.6-7.5°. 20-60 mm band is similar (real 7.8-36°, sim 6.7-9.4°). Visual: corkscrew LAD/LCx in cdm-00884 (RAO caudal/cranial/AP cranial montages).
gaps.proposal: Replace the wiggle block in buildCoronaryTree with a band-limited 3D tortuosity field (new tortuosity.ts). For each vessel, generate lateral offsets in the local surface frame (in-surface normal plus the h direction, so projections differ by view) as three octaves: 3-8, 8-20 and 20-60 mm wavelengths. Seed by patient; draw amplitude from a per-patient tortuosity index (age/hypertension) and vessel class. Add an optional helical 'corkscrew' mode. Enforce a minimum radius of curvature, keep ostia and stented segments straighter, and preserve arc-length parametrisation so lesion positions do not drift. Calibrate so the 8-20 mm band RMS of projected traces lands around 6-22° (median about 11°) and the 3-8 mm band exceeds the measured noise floor by the observed margin. Validate with the shape scripts.

gaps.gap: The heart frame tilts the base plane so the anterior AV/interventricular groove lies above the left main ostium. The fixed polyline plus Hermite bridge therefore makes the LAD and LCx climb and fold back, and the proximal RCA zig-zags off the ostium. These are unanatomical kinks seen in every view.
gaps.evidence: Probe of samplePos: LM bifurcation at y=12.7 mm and LM ostium at y=15. The LAD rises to y=27.2 at sample 15 (14.5 mm above the bifurcation, 12 mm above the ostium) before descending; the LCx rises to y=23.8 (+11.1 mm). The heart frame anterior axis A=(0,0.6,0.8), so at ell=-0.9 the phi=0 groove point sits at y=+20.4 and phi=45 at y=+26.1. Projected sim views show a Z-shaped LM-LAD/LCx junction (RAO caudal, LAO cranial) and an RCA ostial zig-zag (LAO); real montages (24 runs viewed) show smooth proximal courses. The LCx projected in RAO caudal has arc/chord 7.5 because of the fold-back. Ostium heights: sim LM 15 mm versus RCA 12 mm above the valve plane, whereas Philip 2015 (CT, severe AS) found the annulus-to-LM distance smaller than annulus-to-RCA.
gaps.proposal: Define the AV groove as an explicit 3D closed curve (mitral plus tricuspid annular ring) wrapped behind and below the aortic root, and the interventricular grooves as surface curves on the new heart shape. Anchor the LAD origin in the AIV groove beside the pulmonary trunk at or below LM height, and the LCx in the left AV groove under the LAA. Replace the Hermite bridge with a curvature-limited clothoid/spline that leaves along the ostial direction and is monotone in height, unless a variant asks otherwise. Run the RCA in the right AV groove from the ostium with no fixed straight stub. Raise the RCA ostium relative to the LM in anatomy.ts (sample both heights). Add tests: max height over the first 20 mm of LAD/LCx ≤ bifurcation + 3 mm, and maximum turning angle per mm near ostia.

gaps.gap: Every patient has the same tree: fixed node lists, 3 diagonals, 5 septals, 2 OMs, 1 RV branch, 1 AM, and 22-24 random parallel 'twigs' per main vessel. Several named branches are missing, and only dominance plus four variants change the geometry.
gaps.evidence: Eight case seeds give LAD projected length 156.2-157.1 mm and arc/chord 1.299-1.306 (simshape.ts); only wiggle phase and twigs differ. Twigs: about 28 mm long, both sides on the epicardium, mean diameter 0.95 mm on the RCA; septal-side twigs do not enter the septum, and they form the 'comb' visible in the app capture datasets/tmp/captures/test_pci_rao_cran.png. No SA-nodal, AV-nodal, left-atrial or PDA septal branches. The X-ray tree reads only long-lm, short-lm, separate-ostia (drawn as a 4 mm LM) and ramus. Population data opened: dominance right/left/co 81.2/9.1/9.7% (Knaapen 2012, 1453 post-mortem angiograms); 346/54 right/left in CoronaryDominance's random 400-study subset (local DATASET_DESCRIPTION.md; codominance folded into right); intermediate artery in about 30% (Medrano-Gracia 2017) and ramus 32% (Manpoong 2023); diagonals single/double/multiple 14/62/24% and marginals 20/51/29% (Manpoong); wrap-around LAD 86% (Manpoong), 871/1095 anterior-STEMI LAD culprits (Kobayashi 2015), 57% (Ilia 2014); SA-nodal artery from RCA 68.0%, LCx 22.1%, duplicated 4.3% (Vikse 2016); LM length 10.5±5.3 mm and LMB angle 75±23° without / 89±21° with an intermediate artery (Medrano-Gracia 2016). Branch density at the ≥0.7 mm level is not the problem: median vessel crossings per mid-tree transect, real (contrast-only subtraction) 8/7/4 in RAO cranial/AP cranial/LAO cranial (n=15/14/10) versus sim 6/5/5-6.
gaps.proposal: Introduce an AnatomyGenome (new coronaryAtlas.ts) sampled from a case seed, with each prior commented with its source. It covers dominance, LM length/angle, ramus, diagonal/OM/RV-branch counts and origins, wrap-around, SA-nodal origin, conus origin (RCA versus separate ostium), myocardial bridge, sex (Dodge -9% calibre in women) and LVH (+17%). Growth (new coronaryGrowth.ts): route named branches as geodesics on the heart surface towards territory attractors. Diagonals go to the anterolateral wall; septals into the septal plane (h<0); OMs along the obtuse margin; RV branches across the RV free wall; the PDA in the posterior IV groove with inferior septals; PLV branches; an AV-nodal U-turn at the crux; the SA-nodal branch towards the SVC-RA junction. Fill the fine scale by space colonisation constrained to the epicardium and septum, avoiding parallel combs. Keep the TreeVessel API (name, fillId, lesionId, samples, radii, pathMm, param, parent) so lesions, collaterals, scaffolds and PCI wiring keep working. Store each case's genome so a teaching case can say 'ramus present, wrap-around LAD'.

gaps.gap: The rendered heart shadow (ellipsoids in thorax.ts) is not the surface the coronaries ride on and does not beat. The obtuse-margin vessels float well inside the silhouette and the RCA pokes outside it, while the lung is carved around a 16-20 mm fat halo.
gaps.evidence: Radial distances from the long axis (consist.ts): at phi=90 (obtuse margin) the vessels are 8-12 mm inside the myocardial ellipsoid and 24-29 mm inside HEART_FAT, which defines the lung carve. At phi=-90 near the base the RCA is 9 mm outside the myocardial ellipsoid (60.1 vs 51.1 mm). Posterior vessels are 4-9 mm inside. buildThorax receives only resp and heartShift, so the silhouette never changes with contraction while the vessels do. Real frame cdm-00909-LCA-2 frame 44 (zoomed with a grid): a marginal/diagonal branch runs within about 1 mm of the heart-lung border. App renders show a crisp circular heart disc in LAO views.
gaps.proposal: Create one geometric source, heartShape.ts: a parametric biventricular surface (LV truncated prolate spheroid, RV crescent, RVOT/PA trunk, RA/RAA, LA/LAA, aortic root) carrying the groove curves the coronaries use. Each frame, deform it with heartMotion and fit the renderer's analytic primitives to it: about 8-12 ellipsoids/capsules via a small least-squares fit on the CPU, or precomputed per-phase tables, so the exact-interval shader and its frame budget are unchanged. Use a thin 2-4 mm epicardial fat shell with thicker AV-groove and cardiophrenic fat pads instead of the uniform HEART_FAT halo. Only if analytic unions look too blobby, ray-march a 64³ SDF texture for the heart alone (≈64 steps at 768² stays inside a 15 f/s laptop budget). Test: projected marginal arteries lie within 2-3 mm of the silhouette in the standard views.

gaps.gap: Radii follow a smooth per-vessel power-law taper unrelated to branching. Main vessels barely step down after large side branches, so daughter diameters are too large for the parent, and left-dominant LCx calibre is not scaled.
gaps.evidence: Sim bifurcations: D1 parent 3.08 mm → main 2.97 + side 2.51 (Murray cube ratio 1.43, Finet ratio 0.563); OM1 1.55/0.545; OM2 1.70/0.528; PL2 1.44/0.561. Finet 2008: Dm = 0.678(Dd1+Dd2) in 173 normal bifurcations. Medrano-Gracia 2017: most normal bifurcations cluster below Finet's 0.678 boundary and the Huo-Kassab exponential model fits best. Huo/Kassab group (Gong 2016): flow-diameter exponent 7/3. Dodge 1992: LCx proximal 4.2±0.6 mm when left-dominant (sim 3.4 mm regardless), women 9% smaller, LVH +17%.
gaps.proposal: Compute calibres top-down from territory flow. Give each terminal branch a weight proportional to the myocardial mass it serves (from the growth step), accumulate flows to the root, and set D ∝ Q^(3/7). Scale the root so the LM matches Dodge (4.5±0.5 mm, sex/LVH-adjusted). Downstream of each side branch: D_main = (D_parent^(7/3) - D_side^(7/3))^(3/7). Use only a mild taper between branches and keep the existing irregularity drift. Lesion, stent and occlusion logic stay as multiplicative modifiers.

gaps.gap: Quiet breathing is shallower than the lower limit of normal and is a pure rigid translation with a fixed period; no rotation, regional variation or irregularity.
gaps.evidence: sceneBuilder: resp = 0.22*(0.5-0.5cos(2πt/4.3)), so diaphragm excursion is 0.22×32 = 7 mm and the heart shift is (0, -0.85·32·resp, 3·resp) with weight 0.45 at the root. Boussuges 2009 (210 healthy adults, M-mode): quiet-breathing lower limits about 0.9 cm in women and 1.0 cm in men; deep breathing about 3.7/4.7 cm. Wang 1995: heart respiratory motion is dominated by SI, linear in diaphragm SI motion, approximately a global translation. Shechter 2006: on inspiration the arteries move caudally; LR/AP motion variable; breathing motion more complex than a 3D translation.
gaps.proposal: Per-patient breathing parameters: rate, tidal depth sampled at or above normal limits, breath-to-breath variability, sinus-arrhythmia coupling to HR. Heart displacement = SI × patient factor linear in diaphragm descent, plus small patient-specific AP/LR terms and a rotation about the LR axis, with the root still partly tethered. Model a breath-hold state with slow drift and an end-hold release. Make inspiration hold for cranial views (after the sign fix) visibly move the diaphragm off the heart.

gaps.gap: Several AnatomyVariant values do not change the X-ray coronary tree, and clinically important anomalies are absent. Most notable: myocardial bridging with systolic milking, separate LAD/LCx ostia, shepherd's crook RCA, tortuous RCA and anomalous origins.
gaps.evidence: specsFor in coronaryTree.ts never reads model.leftOstium2; the LCx always starts from the LM end point. 'shepherds-crook-rca' and 'tortuous-rca' only alter the old engagement polyline in anatomy.ts, not the rendered tree. No reference to bridging anywhere in src/render/xray. Hostiuc 2018 meta-analysis: myocardial bridging prevalence 6% at angiography, 22% on CT, 42% at autopsy; 82% on the LAD; mean length 19.3 mm; mean thickness 2.47 mm.
gaps.proposal: Map every variant to geometry in the genome. Separate ostia: the LCx starts from leftOstium2 with its own short trunk. Shepherd's crook: a superior proximal RCA loop built with the curvature-limited spline. Tortuous RCA: a high tortuosity index. Myocardial bridge: a 15-25 mm mid-LAD segment at h<0 whose radius is scaled per frame by a systolic compression factor tied to heartMotion phase, so 'milking' appears in cine and interacts with wires and stents. Add anomalous-origin variants (LCx from the right sinus or RCA; RCA from the left sinus with interarterial course) with matching engagement targets.

gaps.area: Heart size, orientation and vessel lengths
gaps.gap: One heart (makeHeart(1)) with a fixed long-axis direction and size for all patients. The projected tree is narrower and taller than real in standard views, and 3D vessel lengths sit at the high end of reported values.
gaps.evidence: Real vessel-mask extents (p2-p98, contrast-only subtraction, 6F scale) versus sim projections in true geometry: LCA RAO caudal 101×98 vs 84×91 mm; RAO cranial 103×94 vs 85×103; AP cranial 94×93 vs 74×115. Real projected LM+LAD length in RAO cranial was 96-136 mm in 5 traces (median 135) versus 144 mm sim. Sim 3D lengths: LAD 169, LCx 101 (right-dominant), RCA 131 mm. Manpoong 2023 angiographic means: LAD 109±14 and LCx 66±12 mm (measured in 2D, so not directly comparable). Real 512-px frames correspond to about 157 mm at the catheter plane (6F), against 165 mm at the iso-centre for the 230 mm default field. Uncertainty: about 17% between 5F and 6F calibration.
gaps.proposal: Make heart size scale with sex/BSA and add long-axis azimuth/elevation/roll plus a few shape modes to the genome (shape-mode ideas from the open four-chamber cohorts of Strocchi 2020 and Rodero 2021; check their licences before using any meshes). Remove the proximal detour (separate gap), then validate projected extent and length distributions against the library per view with the harness. Agree the default field size with the imaging work so on-screen magnification matches typical cine.

gaps.gap: Thoracic anatomy is identical across patients and built from coarse primitives. Pulmonary vessel trees come from a fixed seed, the descending aorta has no explicit tube, rib bands end abruptly, and great-vessel and atrial borders are single ellipsoids.
gaps.evidence: thorax.ts pulmonaryTrees uses prng(7) for every case. The descending aorta exists only inside the POST_MEDIA ellipsoid, although aorticCourse already defines its path for the catheter. Rib tubes stop at thetaEnd with flat ends; the app capture datasets/tmp/captures/test_pci_rao_cran.png shows rectangular rib segments, whereas real frames (e.g. the RAO cranial montage) show oblique curved ribs. Habitus is not linked to heart size or orientation.
gaps.proposal: Seed all thorax structures from the patient genome: rib-cage shape, diaphragm height, lung size and pulmonary trees per patient. Add the aortic arch and descending aorta as soft-tissue/blood tubes along aorticCourse, plus SVC/IVC, with the PA trunk and hilar arteries continuous with the pulmonary trees. Taper rib ends into the costal cartilage. Let habitus drive heart orientation (horizontal heart in large habitus) through the genome. Low cost: a few more tubes and ellipsoids in existing passes.

gaps.gap: No real patient anatomies: all geometry is hand-authored, although the project already holds CC0 multi-view cines with C-arm angles from about 200 patients.
gaps.evidence: datasets/library/dominance-main: 196 patients, 1199 runs with primary/secondary angles (DICOM 0018,1510/1511), typically several LCA views (RAO/AP/LAO × cranial/caudal) and RCA views per study. DATASET_DESCRIPTION.md: views are not synchronised and no SID/SOD is stored. The scratch tools already do minimal-path centreline tracing with snapping, catheter-calibrated widths, cardiac-phase detection by NCC tracking of vessel landmarks, and band and length metrics.
gaps.proposal: Offline pipeline scripts/angio_library/reconstruct3d.mjs. Per patient: (1) pick end-diastolic frames per view from the tracked motion signal; (2) semi-automatically trace the main vessels and named branches and detect bifurcations; (3) match across ≥2 views at least 30° apart using topology plus epipolar constraints from the stored angles, with SID/SOD and table offsets solved by bundle adjustment under priors; (4) triangulate 3D centrelines with radii from catheter-scaled edge widths; (5) map onto heartShape surface coordinates (ell, phi, h) by closest-point projection; (6) save as genome JSON in datasets/library/derived/trees3d/. The runtime can then mix real-derived anatomies with the statistical generator, and heartMotion animates both. Cite Kruzhilov et al. (CC0, attribution not required but courteous).

gaps.gap: Nothing in the repo tests anatomical or kinematic realism, so regressions like the cranial/caudal inversion, proximal kinks, reversed twist or vanishing tortuosity go unnoticed.
gaps.evidence: src/render/xray/xray.test.ts and src/simulation/projection.test.ts only check finiteness or that projections differ. The scratch tools reproduce every number in this audit headlessly in seconds. Simulator side: simgeom.ts, simshape.ts, simmotion.ts, simraster.ts, consist.ts. Real-library side: trace.mjs, track.mjs, shape.mjs, spectrum.mjs, transect2.mjs, cathwidth.mjs.

measurements.what: Catheter shaft width in the CoronaryDominance library (image-scale calibration)
measurements.value: Median 6.5 px (IQR 6.0-6.75, p10 5.25, p90 7.25) over 1072 of 1303 runs. That is 0.31 mm/px if 6 F (2.0 mm), 0.26 mm/px if 5 F; a 512-px frame is about 157 mm (6F) or 131 mm (5F) at the catheter plane.
measurements.method: cathwidth.mjs: in the mid-run frame, chain dark valleys (depth ≥18 grey levels) from the top edge down 70 rows; edge-to-edge width = distance between max-gradient points on 4×-supersampled perpendicular profiles averaged over 5 px; accept runs with IQR ≤1.5 px. Manual check on cdm-00931-LCA-1 frame 30 gave 7.0 px.

measurements.what: Small-scale tortuosity of real versus simulated main vessels
measurements.value: 8-20 mm wavelength band RMS of tangent angle: real LAD (RAO cranial, 5 runs) 7.7-22.4° (median 11.2°); real RCA (LAO, 4 runs) 6.5-12.4°; sim LAD 2.0-2.1°, sim RCA 1.2-1.7°; catheter-shaft noise floor 1.7-3.9°. 3-8 mm band: real 9.0-18.6°, sim 0.2-0.9°, catheter floor 6.6-7.5°. 20-60 mm band: real 7.8-35.9°, sim 6.7-9.4°.
measurements.method: trace.mjs: Dijkstra minimal path on cost 1/(1+vesselness)² between hand-placed waypoints (snap radius 3 px, spur removal) on peak-opacification frames, checked visually on overlays. spectrum.mjs: 1 mm resampling, 2 mm-chord tangent angle, difference of moving averages (±1/±4/±10/±30 mm). Sim: identical code on perspective projections of the simulator's LAD (true RAO 30 cranial 25) and RCA (LAO 28) in mm at the iso-centre (simspec.ts). Real runs: cdm-00884-LCA-3, cdm-00909-LCA-2, cdm-00956-LCA-4, cd-01033-LCA-3, cd-01051-LCA-5, cd-01030-RCA-5, cd-01032-RCA-5, cd-01046-RCA-6, cd-01053-RCA-5.

measurements.what: Cardiac in-plane displacement of real RCA versus LAD and simulator equivalents
measurements.value: Real P10-P90 displacement: RCA (LAO) median 17.8 mm (IQR 11.1-23.2), n=19 landmarks in 4 runs; LAD (RAO cranial) 8.2 mm (5.8-11.7), n=24 in 5 runs; ratio 2.2. Real proximal (10%) landmarks 6-25 mm. Sim ED-to-ES projected: RCA at 10/30/50/70/90% = 1.3/11.7/11.3/10.9/10.7 mm; LM+LAD = 0.7/10.5-11.1/7.3-8.2/3.3-4.9/0.4-1.5 mm; LM 0 mm.
measurements.method: track.mjs: landmarks at 10-90% along the traced centrelines, NCC block matching on vesselness maps (template 41×41, search ±30 px for RCA and ±16 px for LAD), sub-pixel parabola; frames kept only when local vesselness energy >50% of the reference and NCC >0.5; robust P10-P90 range along the principal motion axis; px→mm at 0.31 mm/px (6F). Sim: simmotion.ts sampling contraction() over the cycle with makeCamera geometry.

measurements.what: Real versus simulated coronary in-plane speeds (frame-to-frame at 15 f/s)
measurements.value: Real median speed: RCA 48 mm/s, LAD 17 mm/s; 90th-percentile per landmark (median) RCA 104 mm/s, LAD 38 mm/s; static-landmark noise floor 4.6 mm/s. Sim (72 bpm, sampled at 15 f/s): median 0-5 mm/s per landmark, 90th percentile 43-72 mm/s on moving segments.
measurements.method: Speeds from the same NCC tracks (px/frame × 0.31 mm/px × 15); noise floor from a landmark stuck on static anatomy in cd-01030-RCA-5 (P10-P90 4.9 px). Sim from simspeed.ts.

measurements.what: Fraction of the cardiac cycle with near-zero motion (speed <25% of the 95th-percentile speed)
measurements.value: Sim 0.53 / 0.56 / 0.60 at 60 / 72 / 90 bpm (rises with HR because the envelope is in phase units: onset 0.09, peak 0.38, back to <5% at 0.545 of the cycle). Real tracked landmarks: median 0.39 (RCA) and 0.42 (LAD); real values are biased low by tracking noise.
measurements.method: simquiet.ts on contraction(); period.mjs on real track series.

measurements.what: Vessel branch density (vessels crossing mid-tree horizontal transects)
measurements.value: Real LCA, contrast-only (peak minus pre-contrast vesselness): median 8 (RAO cranial, n=15 runs), 7 (AP cranial, n=14), 4 (LAO cranial, n=10). Sim synthetic images at the same scale, contrast and noise: 6, 5 and 5-6 (6 seeds each).
measurements.method: transect2.mjs: vesselness (15×15 mean minus 3×3 mean), subtraction of a dilated pre-contrast frame, hysteresis mask, 5 transects at 30-70% of the mask's vertical extent, peaks >7 counted. simraster.ts: projected sim tree rasterised at 0.3077 mm/px, attenuation 0.162/mm chord, 3×3 blur, Gaussian noise SD 3.2, same counter.

measurements.what: Extent of the opacified left coronary tree
measurements.value: Real (p2-p98 of vessel mask, 6F scale): RAO caudal 101×98 mm (n=12), RAO cranial 103×94 (n=9), AP cranial 94×93 (n=11), LAO cranial 102×78 (n=8). Sim, true geometry: RAO caudal 84×91, RAO cranial 85×103, AP cranial 74×115, LAO cranial 74×112.
measurements.method: realskel.mjs masks; simext.ts projected sample points of vessels with r0 ≥0.4 mm, mm at the iso-centre plane.

measurements.what: Projected LM+LAD length in RAO cranial
measurements.value: Real 96-136 mm across 5 runs (median 135) at the 6F scale; sim 143.6 mm in true RAO 30 cranial 25 geometry (157 mm with the current inverted sign).
measurements.method: shape.mjs arc length after 1 mm resampling and smoothing of the traced centrelines; simshape.ts for the sim (8 seeds: 143.5-144.5 mm).

measurements.what: Cranial/caudal sign check in the simulator
measurements.value: For cranialCaudal=+30 the detector direction has y=-0.50 (towards the feet). AP projected LAD length 125 mm at +30 versus 134 mm at -30 (orthographic). Sim LAO 33/+27 projects as a compact spider; LAO 33/-27 matches real LAO cranial runs (cdm-00893-LCA-4 and three others). App renders confirmed: the SPIDER preset shows a long vertical LAD; LAO CRA and AP CRA presets show compact trees with no diaphragm.
measurements.method: cc.ts using cameraBasis/makeCamera; simproj.ts rasterised projections compared visually with real montages; live renders through the app's __pciDraw dev hook in a background browser tab (closed afterwards).

measurements.what: Proximal LAD/LCx climb and ostial heights in the simulator
measurements.value: LM bifurcation at y=12.7 mm, LM ostium y=15.0. LAD maximum y=27.2 mm at sample 15 (+14.5 mm above the bifurcation); LCx maximum y=23.8 at sample 18 (+11.1 mm). Groove point at ell=-0.9: phi=0 y=+20.4, phi=45 y=+26.1. RCA ostium 12 mm vs LM 15 mm above the valve plane.
measurements.method: probe.ts evaluating samplePos for every sample of the built tree (right-dominant default case).

measurements.what: Coronary surface versus rendered heart silhouette (simulator)

audits.summary:
WHY IT FEELS LIKE A GAME (diagnosis from the code)
1. The screen gives you the answer instead of making you read the patient. A live coach line ("Good selective left main engagement...", engagement.ts 343-350) sits at the top of the side panel (Simulator.tsx 238-243). Status chips say Engaged / Pressure clean / Dissection (Simulator.tsx 150-157), and raw state codes such as "selective-lm" are shown (CoachPanel.tsx 65). There are PUSH/TWIST/RESIST meters and an exact "tip N°" readout (CatheterHub.tsx 236-328), and fluoro banners such as "TORQUE WHIP" and "TIP IN LV, withdraw" (FluoroView.tsx 627-654). The wire stage has a TARGET dial reading "AIM THE TIP" (ProcedureLab.tsx 655-699). In the PCI lab you get the wire position in mm with "across the lesion", the device-to-lesion offset, and an exact QCA after every injection (AngioPci.tsx 275-283, 366-370, 394-398).
2. Actions are buttons and steps, not hands on devices. WASD/QE keys and dragging anywhere on the image drive the catheter. PCI uses "push 5" buttons and 20° torque steps that take effect instantly (angioPci.ts 521-523). Devices come from dropdowns and go on with a "Load on the wire" button; the indeflator is a range slider plus an Inflate button. The access wire, sheath and catheter tracking are progress bars. Catheters swap instantly on keys 1-9.
3. Device mechanics are tip-based. computeTip places the tip on a cylinder model of the root. The shaft is a Hermite curve fitted backwards from the tip (helpers.ts 67-122), so it never pushes or supports anything. Engagement is a thresholded classifier, and "difficulty" widens the thresholds (engagement.ts 214-218); in reality difficulty comes from the patient's anatomy, not from how forgiving the target is. In the diagnostic lab the wire is a straight line along the tip direction (FluoroView.tsx 136-139), and choosing a different wire changes nothing (store setWire, 381).
4. Contrast and haemodynamics are canned. Pressing Space starts the beam and a fixed bolus together: 4.8 s, 7 mL (useSimulatorStore.ts 617; contrast.ts 38). The PCI lab turns fluoro on for 0.9 s after every action by itself (AngioPci.tsx 94-97). Pressures are fixed numbers that are the same for every patient (pressure.ts 17-106). The heartbeat in the image runs on its own default 72 bpm clock, not in step with the ECG (FluoroView passes no heartRate). VF goes away with one click. The PCI lab has no ECG or pressure monitor at all.
5. Scores and rewards are game mechanics. A score bar is visible during the case (CoachPanel.tsx 79). Finishing earns XP (useProgressStore.ts 95), levels have titles from "Aortic Root Novice" to "CathMaster" (curriculum.ts 165-176), and there is a day streak (App.tsx 191-193). Hints cost points, and Reset and Try again are always available.
6. There is no team, no conscious patient, and none of the real set-up: time-out, heparin, cocktail, double flush, manifold, zeroing.

WHAT THE REAL ANGIOGRAMS SHOW (measured on 2,005 real runs with Pillow; methods below)
- A real diagnostic study has about 4-5 LCA runs and 1-3 RCA runs. The simulator counts 2 (or 4) diagnostic injections as enough.
- Operators fine-tune the C-arm angle per patient: in 88-89% of runs at least one angle is off a 5° grid. The PCI lab only has fixed preset buttons.
- The cine pedal comes before the injection. Contrast was never present in the first frame of any of 1,314 Philips runs, and arrives at a median 0.73-0.8 s. The simulator injects the moment acquisition starts (arrival 0.33 s, identical every run).
- Operators often stop filming early: 39-48% of Philips LCA runs end while opacification is still above half its peak. Every simulator run plays its full fixed timeline to complete washout.
- The image moves during the run (respiration or table pan), sustained for a cardiac cycle in 9-21% of Philips runs and 52-73% of CADICA runs. The simulator holds the patient's breath at a fixed level throughout cine.
- How long contrast stays above half its peak varies from run to run (Philips LCA q10-q90 0.93-2.27 s). In the simulator it is the same every time (3.07 s diagnostic, 2.4 s PCI), because the user has no control over the injection.

WHAT THE USER'S REFERENCES ADD
- SimCath (Imperial College): a portable simulated cath lab with a motorised mock C-arm and a multi-port haptic interface, software ported to Unity, and a "theatre set" approach to the environment. Their related research covers inextensible Cosserat-rod catheters and wires calibrated against CT-scanned phantoms (VCSim3, 2017), mass-spring wires matched to measured bending stiffness, and team training with actor patients, where patient anxiety ratings differed with operator experience (Kelay 2018). The lesson for us: contextual fidelity (team, patient, environment) matters as much as image fidelity, and instrument physics should be calibrated against real measurements.
- Philips coronary suite (vendor page, claims are the vendor's own): what a modern operator expects at the table. That includes motion-compensated roadmap guidance, iFR physiology and IVUS co-registration in one workspace, single tableside touchscreen control, and a flexible C-arm. We should build generic equivalents (reference image, physiology and imaging at the table) without copying any vendor's UI.
- Evidence that mentored simulation transfers to real cases: Bagai 2012 RCT, Popovic 2019 RCT, Heart-SIMS-1 2026.

THE DESIGN: HOW IT MUST FEEL REAL
The organising idea is one continuous case session per patient on a single clock. It runs from arrival through time-out, access, diagnostic runs, ad hoc PCI and closure to handover. Everything in it is physically coupled, and nothing is a button that teleports the state.
- Devices are elastic rods (catheter, wire, sheath, balloon) inside a vessel lumen, solved by XPBD in a Web Worker, so engagement, deep seating, prolapse, wire migration and guide back-out emerge from the physics.
- Hand injection runs through a manifold and syringe. Injection flow is compared with phasic coronary flow from physiology.ts, which produces streaming, reflux, hang-up and catheter recoil.
- Pressure comes from the tip location plus a second-order transducer chain with zeroing, levelling and air damping.
- The patient's physiology and a 12-lead ECG respond to contrast, occlusion, vagal triggers, spasm, adenosine and VF, and VF needs real management.
- The cine and fluoro pedals are independent of the injection.
- Team and patient agents talk with closed-loop communication.
- An attending mentor that you can switch to silent replaces the HUD. Debrief is an event-sourced replay with deterministic rewind-and-branch.

INTERACTION MODEL WITHOUT HAPTIC HARDWARE
- Right hand is the mouse, in pointer lock with unadjustedMovement and a calibrated mm per count. Hold the button to grip the device you are holding. Moving the mouse forward or back pushes or pulls 1:1. Moving it sideways rolls the device, with angular gain 2s/D for the diameter being rolled, so a torque device gives finer control. Each grip has a limited roll before you must regrip, and releasing lets stored twist spin the hub back.
- Left hand is held keys that pin the wire or the guide ("I have the wire"). If the wire is not pinned, advancing a balloon drags it forward.
- The syringe plunger and the indeflator screw are explicit grips. Their resistance is felt through pseudo-haptic gain taken from the physics forces at the hub.
- Feet are F (fluoro) and C (cine), or USB/MIDI/HID foot switches.
- Optional inputs: a gamepad, where the sticks drive the C-arm and table at limited speed and rumble follows contact force; trackpad two-axis scrolling for the roll and push channel; and push-to-talk speech commands to the team, with a typed command palette as fallback.
- Audio: monitor beeps locked to the QRS, an exposure tone while the beam is on, syringe and indeflator sounds, and the patient's voice.

WHAT TO REMOVE
Mid-case scores, the meters and banners, the tip-angle readout, the TARGET dial, ground-truth coach strings, automatic QCA, mm read-outs, XP, levels and streaks, hint penalties, mid-case reset, and difficulty-as-tolerance. Replace them with:
- a logbook with entrustment decisions per procedure type;
- segment-coverage and dose/contrast debriefs;
- "rewind to a decision point" in place of Try again.

The 26 gaps below give per-file engine and UI changes, ranked by impact and effort.

gaps.area: Imaging workflow: pedals, injection and runs
gaps.gap: Cine and contrast injection are one action with a fixed timeline, and the PCI lab turns fluoro on by itself after every action. The operator never coordinates pedal, breath-hold and injection, and never decides how long to film.
gaps.evidence: In the diagnostic lab, useSimulatorStore.inject() starts the bolus and the beam together with a fixed duration of 4.8 s or 3.4 s (src/state/useSimulatorStore.ts 492-635, line 617); volume is fixed at 7 mL (src/simulation/contrast.ts 38). In the PCI lab, act() sets live.current.until = now + 900 on every action (src/ui/sections/AngioPci.tsx 94-97) and cine lasts a fixed 4.2 s (line 475). Running the real sceneBuilder code (esbuild bundle in scratch) gives the same curve on every run: 30%-of-rise arrival 0.33 s after cine start, plateau 3.07 s (diagnostic) or 2.4 s (PCI), always ending fully washed out. Real Philips runs (n=1,314): contrast was never present in the first frame; median arrival was 0.73-0.8 s; 39-48% of LCA runs ended with opacification still above half its peak.
gaps.proposal: 1) Make three independent inputs: fluoro pedal (hold F or foot switch), cine pedal (hold C or second switch), and syringe (right-hand grip, see the injection-physics gap). 2) The image updates only while a pedal is held, in both labs. Delete the AngioPci live.current.until auto-exposure, and reuse FluoroView's last-image-hold logic in PciFluoro by extracting a shared LiveMonitor component. 3) A run is the interval the cine pedal is held. On release, push a CineSeries {id, frames: ImageBitmap[], fps, cArm, field, panMm, doseMGy, kapGycm2, injectedMl, t0} into a new useSeriesStore for review and a reference image. 4) Breath-hold becomes a spoken command to the patient (team-agents gap), not a constant. 5) Fluoro and cine have separate frame rates and dose rates (dose gap). 6) The mentor's rubric checks the sequence pedal, then breath, then inject, then release once the distal bed has filled.

gaps.gap: No syringe, manifold, injection rate or force. Opacification does not depend on how you inject, so there are no test puffs, no streaming from a weak injection, no graded reflux, no hang-up in a wedged catheter, and no catheter recoil.
gaps.evidence: sceneBuilder computes concentration as 350*(0.55+0.35*b.peak), with a front at a constant 115 mm/s scaled only by flowFactor (src/render/xray/sceneBuilder.ts 172-205). Stenosis delay is a heuristic slow factor (lines 190-197). Injection outcome is a categorical switch on engagement state (src/simulation/contrast.ts 32-154). PCI inject() adds a fixed 8 or 6 mL (src/simulation/angioPci.ts 705-708). The local Oxford handbook notes (docs/reference/Coronary Angiography - Oxford Specialist Handbook.docx) describe test puffs of a few mL, LCA 5-10 mL and RCA 3-5 mL, de-airing the syringe tilted up, and streaming when pressure is insufficient. Measured real plateau varies run to run (Philips LCA q10-q90 0.93-2.27 s); the simulator's is constant.
gaps.proposal:
New src/simulation/injection.ts.
1) ManifoldState {tap: 'pressure'|'contrast'|'flush'|'waste'; syringe {volMl, contrastMl, salineMl, bloodMl, airMl}; lineAirMl}.
2) Plunger velocity comes from the right-hand grip. Injection flow Q_inj is limited by catheter resistance (Poiseuille from French size, length and contrast viscosity) and by hand force; resistance is felt as pseudo-haptic gain. This captures the handbook point that 4-5F catheters need more force.
3) Tip mixing each physics step, with coronary flow Q_cor(t) from physiology.ts flow() and compression(phase):
   - If Q_inj >= Q_cor*open: vessel inlet concentration is C0, and reflux (Q_inj - Q_cor*open) goes to the sinus/root plume.
   - Otherwise inlet concentration is C0*Q_inj/(Q_inj+Q_cor*open), giving streaming.
   - Here open is the fraction of the ostium left open by the catheter, from the rod model.
4) Replace the canned front with 1-D upwind advection along each tree vessel's pathMm samples. Velocity = Q/A(s), using the lesion area and Gould losses from physiology.ts, so TIMI-like delay and phasic pulsation emerge.
5) Pass per-sample concentration into the tube mu arrays in sceneBuilder in place of b.peak and injectDur.
6) Jet reaction force ~ rho*Q_inj^2/A_lumen is applied to the catheter tip in the rod solver, so a poorly seated JR backs out on a forceful injection.
7) Aspiration (pull back on the plunger with the tap to the catheter) returns blood only if the tip is free. Air drawn into the syringe appears as bubbles that must be tilted out and expelled. Air injected becomes a coronary air embolism in the complication engine.
8) Calibrate the default expert injection against the measured library timing (arrival 0.73-0.8 s after cine start, plateau median 1.5-1.7 s).

gaps.area: Interaction model: hands, grips and input devices
gaps.gap: Controls are abstract keys, dragging anywhere on the image, and step buttons. There is no notion of which hand holds which device, no grip or regrip, no pinning, and devices never drag each other. It feels like steering a cursor, not handling equipment.
gaps.evidence: Keymap: src/ui/sim/Simulator.tsx 55-92. Dragging the fluoro image drives the catheter: src/ui/sim/FluoroView.tsx 571-583. Hub drag: src/ui/sim/CatheterHub.tsx 79-91. PCI uses W/S as ±2 mm and Q/E as ±20° steps with buttons (src/ui/sections/AngioPci.tsx 112-116, 255-274), and torqueWire applies the rotation instantly (src/simulation/angioPci.ts 521-523). The local Medmastery handbook stresses fixing the wire while sliding the balloon, "I have the wire" communication, and that torque devices change tactile feedback (docs/reference/Medmastery - PCI Essentials Handbook.pdf).
gaps.proposal:
New src/input/ layer.
1) InputSource interface {poll(): HandCommand[]}, with implementations PointerLockMouse (requestPointerLock({unadjustedMovement:true}) per MDN), TrackpadWheel (deltaX/deltaY), GamepadSource (sticks drive C-arm and table velocity; triggers are pedals), MidiPedalSource (Web MIDI), HidPedalSource (WebHID), and KeyboardSource.
2) HandState {right:{device: DeviceId|'syringe'|'indeflator', gripped, rollUsedDeg}, left:{pin:'wire'|'guide'|'sheath'|null}}.
3) While gripped, mouse dy is push/pull at a calibrated 1:1 mm. Mouse dx is roll, theta = 2*dx/D_grip, with D from the gripped object (catheter hub, torque device, balloon shaft). Each grip has a roll span after which you must release and regrip. On release, stored shaft torque unwinds through the hub (shown as the hub rotating back).
4) Switching grips (keys 1-5) takes a short animated hand move. During the switch, an unpinned wire drifts with cardiac motion and friction.
5) Commands go at a fixed rate to the physics worker (rod-physics gap).
6) A one-time calibration screen asks the user to move the mouse a known distance on a ruler.
7) TableView.tsx strip shows the hands, sheath hub, catheter, Y-connector or O-ring, torque device, manifold taps and syringe contents.
8) Retire FluoroView drag-to-steer and the CatheterHub dial.

gaps.area: Device mechanics: catheter, wire and sheath as elastic rods
gaps.gap: The tip is placed analytically and the catheter body is drawn backwards from it, so pushing, support, deep seating, prolapse, loops and wire tracking are scripted rather than physical. Wire choice has no effect, and the access route does not change catheter behaviour.
gaps.evidence: computeTip: tip on a cylinder of height seatHeight-insertion and azimuth from torque (src/simulation/engagement.ts 187-204). Prolapse is a rule: a 3.2 jump when forwardPressure exceeds a threshold (lines 147-157). catheterPath fits Hermite curves from a family contact point to the tip (src/ui/sim/helpers.ts 67-122). The diagnostic wire is a straight segment from the tip (src/ui/sim/FluoroView.tsx 136-139). setWire only stores an id (src/state/useSimulatorStore.ts 381). The roadmap notes access is cosmetic in engagement (docs/UPGRADE_ROADMAP.md A3) and lists rods as still to do (line 45). Imperial's VCSim3 modelled catheters and guidewires as inextensible Cosserat rods calibrated against CT-scanned phantom shapes (Korzeniowski 2017, doi 10.1007/s11548-017-1679-1).
gaps.proposal:
New src/physics/ running in a Web Worker.
1) Rod.ts: discrete Cosserat rod, XPBD stretch/shear, bend/twist and inextensibility constraints. Per-node rest curvature and twist arrays encode each catheter family's preformed shape, defined in data/catheters.ts as a curvature profile rather than reach/azimuth scalars. Per-device bending stiffness profile (shaft, transition, soft tip) and coating friction coefficient (hydrophilic vs PTFE).
2) VesselLumen.ts: centreline Catmull-Rom spline plus radius function. Route from radial or femoral up to the root, seeded from thorax.aorticCourse() polylines. Aortic root as three sinus lobes joined at the commissures, with the valve plane as a one-way barrier that a pushed pigtail or wire can cross. Coronary lumens from coronaryTree vessel samples and radii, so tree and physics share one geometry.
3) Contact: per node, closest-point projection to the lumen wall plus Coulomb friction. Nested rods (wire in catheter in sheath) are constrained to the outer lumen. Hub boundary conditions come from the HandState (interaction-model gap).
4) Output per step: node positions (Float32Array via transferable buffers), hub axial and torsional reaction, tip pose, and contact forces per node. These feed the pseudo-haptic gain, rumble, the complication hazards and the renderer tube ribbons (replacing catheterPath).
5) computeEngagement becomes a read-only classifier of rod geometry (tip inside the ostial lumen, depth, coaxiality) for the mentor and debrief only. Delete difficulty-dependent THRESH (lines 214-218): difficulty should come from anatomy, not tolerance.
6) Budget: physics fixed-step in the worker, decoupled from the 15 fps renderer. Add a benchmark test so node counts adapt to the device.
7) Calibrate rest shapes and stiffness against real catheter silhouettes traced in pre-contrast frames of the CoronaryDominance runs (datasets/library/dominance*).

gaps.gap: Families differ only by scalar parameters plus a seatCue string. The manoeuvre a clinician learns (JR4 clockwise rotation while slowly withdrawing; Tiger anticlockwise in the left sinus; Tiger diving into the RCA) is not reproduced by the mechanics. Any torque toward the right azimuth engages.
gaps.evidence: behaviour {reach, naturalAzimuth, seatHeight, torqueResponse, prolapseTendency, deepEngagementRisk} (src/data/catheters.ts, for example JL4 lines 52-84). Engagement is decided by distance and alignment thresholds (src/simulation/engagement.ts 330-351). The local Oxford handbook notes describe JR4 engagement with gentle clockwise torque while slowly withdrawing, Tiger LCA by anticlockwise rotation in the left sinus, Tiger's dive into the RCA corrected by anticlockwise torque and withdrawal, and JL3.5/JL4/JL5 choice by access and root size.
gaps.proposal:
Once the rod-physics gap is built, encode only the preformed shapes and let the manoeuvres emerge. Add a regression suite src/physics/manoeuvres.test.ts that runs scripted hand trajectories through the solver in Node and asserts geometric outcomes:
- JR4 in the right cusp: clockwise roll with slow withdrawal puts the tip in the RCA ostial lumen, coaxial.
- Tiger: anticlockwise in the left sinus engages the LM; pushing after RCA engagement drives the tip deep.
- JL3.5 vs JL4 vs JL5 across small, normal and dilated roots: the fit changes.
Keep catheters.ts teaching text, but generate mentor phrasing from the rod state (for example 'your tip is pointing posterior; the shaft is loaded with clockwise twist'). Have a clinician review each signature before it becomes a test. Encode only manoeuvres that a source in docs/reference supports.

gaps.area: Pressure transducer chain, haemodynamics and a single cardiac clock
gaps.gap: Pressure is a lookup of fixed numbers that are the same for every patient. There is no manifold, zeroing, levelling, fast-flush test or air damping. The heartbeat in the image runs on its own default clock, not in step with the ECG and pressure traces.
gaps.evidence: computePressure returns constants (122/76 aortic, 86/63 damped, 116/14 ventricularised, 118/7 LV) (src/simulation/pressure.ts 10-107). HEART_PERIOD is a constant 0.84 s (line 148). FluoroView calls buildXrayScene without heartRate, so sceneBuilder uses its default of 72 (src/render/xray/sceneBuilder.ts 154). VitalsMonitor integrates its own heartPhase (src/ui/sim/VitalsMonitor.tsx 88-93). Sources: StatPearls LHC (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK564323/) says the catheter is connected to the manifold and pressures recorded. Deranged Physiology describes zeroing to air, levelling (7.4 mmHg per 10 cm below the axis), damping from air bubbles and long or compliant tubing, and the fast-flush test (https://derangedphysiology.com/main/cicm-primary-exam/cardiovascular-system/Chapter-758/arterial-line-pressure-transducer-setup).
gaps.proposal:
1) A session CardiacClock {t, beatIndex, beatPhase, rr (with sinus arrhythmia and respiratory variation), respPhase} drives the ECG, pressure, physiology.compression() and sceneBuilder's contraction (pass beat phase in place of inp.t*hr/60).
2) Aortic pressure p_ao(t) comes beat by beat from circulation.ts (existing lumped model) with patient-specific parameters.
3) Tip pressure from the rod tip location:
   - In the root: p_ao.
   - In an ostium: a small chamber connected to the aorta through the residual gap conductance (gap area from catheter OD vs ostial lumen and coaxiality) and to the distal bed (physiology.ts resistance). Damping, wedging and ventricularisation then emerge; RCA ventricularisation via conus/RV-branch run-off.
   - In the LV: an LV pressure model.
4) Transducer chain as a second-order system H(s) with natural frequency and damping from tubing length, bubble volume and compliance (ManifoldState.lineAirMl), plus hydrostatic offset from transducer height and a zero offset until zeroed.
5) UI: zero (open to air), level (raise or lower the transducer) and fast-flush square wave on the monitor.
6) Catheter-tip spasm: ostial radius as a state variable driven by contact force, reversed by IC GTN. The handbook describes ventricularisation then a pressure drop, and GTN 100-250 µg.

gaps.gap: The procedure starts at puncture and skips most of the real work: patient check and time-out, sedation, heparin and radial cocktail, sheath flush, catheter-over-wire exchange, back-bleed and double flush, manifold connection, transducer zero, and a pressure check before engagement. A catheter change takes zero time and carries no risk.
gaps.evidence: PHASE_ORDER is puncture, access-wire, sheath, wire-navigate, catheter-track, engage (src/simulation/procedure.ts 29-36). advanceCatheter sets wireRemoved at 100% (src/state/useProcedureStore.ts 144-156). setCatheter resets controls to a seated catheter instantly (src/state/useSimulatorStore.ts 370-379), and number keys swap catheters (src/ui/sim/Simulator.tsx 87-91). Aspiration is a single button (src/ui/sim/CatheterHub.tsx 358-371). Sources: StatPearls LHC (premedication against radial spasm; 5000 IU heparin with nitroglycerin through the sheath; femoral puncture over the femoral head; catheter to manifold, pressures recorded), Medmastery handbook (cocktail of nitrate and verapamil diluted in aspirated blood; ACT 250-350 s for PCI; balloon tracking; wire straying into the descending aorta, corrected in LAO with a deep breath), Oxford notes (aspirate before injecting; air prevention).
gaps.proposal:
Replace the phase stepper with a CaseSession checklist that the trainee drives in any order (src/simulation/session/caseSession.ts).
1) Chart review: allergies, eGFR, anticoagulants, weight.
2) Team time-out by voice or command palette; team agents confirm and log it.
3) Orders: sedation, analgesia, heparin; drug state feeds the patient model and ACT.
4) Exchanges as physical sequences on the rod model: insert J-wire, track catheter, pull wire (back-bleed), aspirate to waste, flush, connect to manifold, zero and level, check the aortic trace. Each step takes real time and can be done badly.
5) Each omission has a consequence through physics or hazards: air in the catheter becomes air embolism; an unzeroed transducer gives wrong numbers; missing heparin raises the hazard of catheter thrombus and radial occlusion at closure.
6) A catheter exchange needs a wire in the aorta. Exchanging without one is allowed, but the mentor flags it and the rod model shows the consequences.

gaps.gap: Puncture is a one-dimensional depth slider with a fixed window on an SVG cartoon. Access wire, sheath and catheter tracking are progress bars. Wire navigation is a 2D schematic with an aim-at-target dial. Engagement then loads a different simulator case.
gaps.evidence: evaluatePuncture uses fixed depth windows (src/simulation/procedure.ts 320-328). PunctureStage SVG (src/ui/sections/ProcedureLab.tsx 196-272). StatPearls gives the radial puncture site 2-3 cm above the wrist crease; Medmastery covers radial spasm triggers and the cocktail.
gaps.proposal:
1) Ultrasound-guided puncture: new src/simulation/access/ultrasound.ts with a synthetic B-mode of artery and venae comitantes (cross-section and long axis, pulsatile artery, compressible veins), needle position, angle and lateral offset, needle reflection and tissue tenting. Flashback in the hub is pulsatile only when the needle tip is in the lumen. Back-wall puncture and subintimal wire are possible.
2) Wire through the needle with resistance coming from the rod model.
3) Sheath with friction. Radial diameter is a state variable that shrinks with contact force and patient anxiety (spasm) and recovers after cocktail; the patient reports pain.
4) Wire navigation on the real X-ray renderer: pan the table to forearm, shoulder and arch, with lumen geometry from the rod-physics gap. Subclavian tortuosity straightens on a deep breath (keep the logic from stepWire). Wire into the descending aorta is corrected in LAO with a deep breath (Medmastery).
5) Delete TipDial and the schematic; the trainee sees only fluoroscopy.
6) Continue into engagement in the same CaseSession with the same catheter and route.

gaps.area: C-arm, table, collimation, reference image and run review
gaps.gap: Views snap instantly to presets, there is no joystick and no table pan in the PCI lab, and there are no collimator shutters or wedges, no stored fluoro, no reference monitor and no run review. The patient's breathing is held perfectly constant during every cine run.
gaps.evidence: applyViewPreset sets angles instantly (src/state/useSimulatorStore.ts 726-729); AngioPci uses preset buttons only (src/ui/sections/AngioPci.tsx 174-183). breathHold is a constant 0.7 during cine (src/ui/sim/FluoroView.tsx 158; AngioPci.tsx 519). Measured: 88-89% of real runs have at least one angle off a 5° grid (374/426 and 1,064/1,199). Sustained global image motion (cardiac-averaged, at least 6.25% of image width) in 9-21% of Philips runs and 52-73% of CADICA runs; contact sheets confirmed pans and diaphragm motion. The Medmastery handbook describes freezing the best lesion frame on a second screen as a reference for wiring.
gaps.proposal:
1) CArmDynamics in src/simulation/imaging/carm.ts: commanded angular velocity from joystick (gamepad stick or held arrows) with acceleration, a speed cap and dead-man stop. Presets become APC memories that drive there while held. Continuous angles shown on the monitor.
2) Table: float pan with inertia during fluoro or cine (mouse with a table key, or right stick), plus height.
3) Collimator shutters and wedge filters as renderer uniforms in XrayRenderer's display and transmission passes: attenuate outside the shutters, reduce scatter and dose with the collimated area.
4) Patient respiration model obeying commands with a delay, inspiration depth and slow drift during the hold, replacing the constant breathHold.
5) Store fluoro (last N seconds of fluoro frames as a series).
6) SeriesBrowser on the reference monitor (thumbnails, loop, frame step, choose reference frame) as a generic reference image. Do not copy vendor motion-compensated overlays.

gaps.area: Physiological responses, ECG and arrhythmia management
gaps.gap: The ECG is a single synthetic lead, and ST changes come only from damping dwell. Contrast never causes bradycardia, there is no vagal reaction, and balloon inflation causes no ischaemia or chest pain (the PCI lab has no monitor). There is no AV block with adenosine. VF happens only with a conus injection and ends with one click.
gaps.evidence: ecgFromSim: HR 71 baseline, ischaemia from obstructing dwell (src/simulation/ecg.ts 75-132). Defibrillate() resets arrhythmia instantly (src/state/useSimulatorStore.ts 671-682); VF button (src/ui/sim/CatheterHub.tsx 374-382). AngioPci has no ECG or pressure. The Medmastery handbook covers adenosine AV-block monitoring and warning the patient; the Oxford notes cover conus injection VF and catheter-tip spasm.
gaps.proposal:
New src/simulation/patient/responses.ts, driven by physics exposures each beat:
- Contrast mass per territory per beat (injection model) and contrast stasis time.
- Occluded myocardium fraction (balloon, wedged guide, dissection, no-reflow) mapped to territories.
- Pain and anxiety from access, cocktail and inflation.
- Vagal tone, and drugs given (GTN, adenosine, atropine, vasopressors).
These produce: HR and rhythm (sinus, brady, AV block, VT, VF, asystole), BP via circulation.ts, territory ST vectors projected onto a 12-lead model (src/simulation/ecg12.ts, lead vectors), patient speech, and SpO2.
VF becomes a management sequence: call it, charge, clear, shock, check rhythm, CPR if delayed. Time to shock affects the downstream state.
Add the haemodynamic monitor to the PCI lab and a 12-lead snapshot on request.
Time courses and magnitudes are calibrated parameters; source each in SIM_FACTS.md before it ships.

gaps.gap: Guide pre-engaged; devices picked from dropdowns and loaded instantly; no rapid-exchange vs over-the-wire, no haemostatic valve, no wire pinning or migration, no guide back-up or back-out; indeflator is a slider with instant inflation; no inflation time, deflation time, melon-seeding, marker-ruler use or contrast-puff positioning.
gaps.evidence: initialPci: 'guide engaged' at t=0 (src/simulation/angioPci.ts 237); loadDevice instant (530-538); inflate() applies the chosen atm at once (565-690); UI selects and 'Load on the wire' button, range slider 2-24 atm (src/ui/sections/AngioPci.tsx 286-365). Medmastery handbook procedural steps: open O-ring and tell staff the trace will vanish; indeflator negative-neutral-inflate reading pressure while watching expansion; melon seeding; markers as a ruler; deflate to full negative watching bubbles; position stent then inject; fix the wire while sliding the balloon; watch the distal wire; check the box label; guide back-wall support.
gaps.proposal: Equipment in the session inventory (src/simulation/session/equipment.ts): DeviceSpec from pciBench BALLOON_SPEC/STENT_SPEC plus delivery {type:'rx'|'otw', profile, pushability, trackability, friction}. Workflow: request via nurse (team agents) -> box with label (check action) -> prep (indeflator negative; balloon air) -> backload onto the externalised wire (wire pinned by left hand) -> open haemostatic valve (tip pressure channel drops out; physiologist comments) -> advance on the rod model with friction; guide reaction force pushes the guide out of the ostium if backup (guide family, engagement depth, rod contact on the opposite aortic wall) is insufficient; unpinned wire migrates distally -> perforation hazard. Indeflator as a grip: screw rate sets pressure rise along pciBench compliance (balloonDiameter), inflation time accrues territory ischaemia (responses), rapid inflation in rubbery lesion -> melon-seed displacement; deflation needs time to full negative. Stent positioning with marker bands, contrast puffs through the guide and proximal branch landmarks; post-dilation NC inside stent; guide extension and buddy wire as options. Debrief metric: distal wire excursion during device advances (wire husbandry).

gaps.gap: Branch entry is a cosine test at each take-off; torque is instantaneous; lesion crossing is binary by wire type; perforation triggers when pushed 1.5 mm past the vessel end.
gaps.evidence: moveWire enters a branch when cos(tipAngle - takeOffAngle) > 0.6 (src/simulation/angioPci.ts 431-441); canCross by wire kind (395-399); perforation at end + 1.5 mm (472-482); torqueWire adds dRad directly (521-523).
gaps.proposal: Coronary wire on the rod solver inside coronaryTree lumens (shared with the device-physics gap): user shapes the tip before insertion (primary/secondary bend angle and length via a 'shape tip' step with the introducer), torque transmitted through guide and proximal bends with lag and whip, tip load and stiffness per wire (workhorse, polymer, tapered CTO) from wires.ts, lesion cap as a resistance field (penetration when tip axial force exceeds cap strength; subintimal track probability rises with tip load and off-axis force), prolapse/knuckle visible in the image, distal migration when devices advance. Branch selection then emerges from tip orientation relative to the take-off in 3D rather than a cosine rule.

gaps.gap: Complications are deterministic thresholds latched as flags, with no prodrome, evolution or in-lab bailout; management is a button or nothing.
gaps.evidence: Dissection when trauma >= 1 (src/state/useSimulatorStore.ts 842-878); air embolism when injecting without the aspirate flag in a risky position (522-551); conus injection -> VF always (499-520); PCI: dissection if balloon/reference > 1.2, rupture if atm > RBP + 2, perforation grades fixed (src/simulation/angioPci.ts 580-645); no tamponade progression or link to the existing pericardiocentesis engine. docs/reference/BRILAKIS_PRINCIPLES.md: prevent -> recognise early -> treat decisively; coronary/cardiac/other taxonomy; complications track already teaches crisis sequences (src/content/tracks/complications.ts 102-119, 397-414).
gaps.proposal: src/simulation/complications/: each complication = {exposures from physics (wall contact force integral, tip injection pressure, oversize ratio, inflation pressure vs RBP, wire tip load in small branches, contrast in conus, air volume), hazard h(exposure), seeded draw (session seed for reproducible replay), prodrome signs (pressure change, patient symptom, image cue), progression model (e.g. perforation leak rate -> pericardial volume -> pressure -> BP via circulation.ts; dissection length grows with injection pressure), management actions with effects (prolonged balloon tamponade, covered stent, protamine, pericardiocentesis via src/simulation/pericardiocentesis.ts, temporary pacing via pacing.ts, defibrillation)}. Team agents participate (role assignment, read-backs) as taught in the complications track.

gaps.gap: No nurse, radiographer, physiologist, anaesthetist or conscious patient; every action is self-service, so closed-loop communication and multitasking with a talking patient (core cath-lab realism) are never practised.
gaps.evidence: No team model anywhere in src/state or src/simulation; drugs and devices are buttons/selects (AngioPci.tsx 286-392). Academy already scripts closed-loop crisis communication (src/content/tracks/complications.ts 102-119). Imperial's cath-lab simulation work used an embedded actor patient and found patient anxiety ratings differed by operator experience and were shaped by tone, continuity and communicating while multitasking (Kelay 2018, doi 10.1136/bmjstel-2017-000249). Medmastery: 'I have the wire', 'O-ring is open wide', never assume the right size was handed over.
gaps.proposal: src/simulation/team/: Agent {role, perception (what they can observe: physiologist = monitor, scrub nurse = table and inventory, radiographer = C-arm/dose, patient = sensations), speech queue with latency, memory}. Inputs: push-to-talk SpeechRecognition (Web Speech API; feature-detected) parsed by an intent grammar (drug, dose, route; device request; breath commands; C-arm/table; 'I have the wire'), with a typed command palette fallback. Outputs: SpeechSynthesis voices + captions; read-backs ('heparin 5,000 units given at 10:32') logged with timestamps; equipment fetch latency; rare wrong-item events requiring a label check; patient speech (pain at puncture, burning with cocktail, chest pain on inflation, nausea in vagal reaction, distress with adenosine). Communication quality (read-backs closed, patient informed before adenosine/inflation) feeds the communication debrief domain.

Mentored simulation transfer evidence: Bagai 2012 RCT (doi 10.1161/CIRCINTERVENTIONS.112.970772), Popovic 2019 RCT (doi 10.1016/j.amjcard.2019.01.032), Heart-SIMS-1 2026 (doi 10.1186/s12909-026-08831-6).
gaps.proposal: 1) Event-sourced SessionLog (input commands at physics rate, downsampled; all state transitions; series; orders), deterministic physics with session seed -> exact replay. 2) Debrief player: scrubber across live/reference monitors, haemodynamics, table view, with auto-detected decision points (first injection, catheter changes, damping events, inflations, complications). 3) 'Rewind and branch' from any decision point (restore snapshot, continue with new inputs) - impossible in real life and the core of deliberate practice. 4) Attending agent: Teach (narrates steps, Socratic questions, 'show me' plays an expert trajectory through the same physics), Supervised (silent; intervenes before predicted harm, e.g. blocks a syringe push onto a ventricularised trace as a hand on yours would), Solo (none). Commentary references Academy lesson ids (src/content) and local handbook statements. 5) Expert ghost: recorded expert sessions on the same case shown as a translucent second rod in replay with metrics (path length, torque reversals, beam-on-while-idle, runs). 6) Auto-generated drills from weaknesses (e.g. JR4 in horizontal roots x10).

gaps.proposal: src/simulation/coverage.ts: for each stored series and each AHA/SYNTAX segment of the tree, compute opacification adequacy (concentration from the injection model above a visibility threshold at end-diastole), foreshortening (angle between segment tangent and detector plane from projection.ts camera), and overlap (minimum projected distance to other opacified segments and the catheter). End of case requires a structured report (dominance, lesions with segment, severity, TIMI) compared with ground truth; QCA only on stored frames by the trainee (leakage gap).

gaps.area: Coronary physiology inside the cath lab
gaps.gap: Pressure-wire physiology exists only in a separate Physiology lab; the PCI lab cannot measure FFR or a non-hyperaemic ratio, equalise, check drift, or give adenosine, and angiographic flow is not driven by the same physiology.
gaps.evidence: physiology.ts implements Gould losses, phasic flow, FFR, wave-free ratio, pullback, drift and guide wedging (src/simulation/physiology.ts 1-318) but AngioPci never imports it; sceneBuilder uses its own stenosis slow-down heuristic (src/render/xray/sceneBuilder.ts 188-197). Medmastery handbook gives the pressure-wire procedure (flush, calibrate, sensor just out of the guide, introducer out and valve closed, equalise to Pd/Pa 1, advance, document, IC nitrate, warn about adenosine, watch AV block, steady state, check back to 1 at the ostium for drift). Thresholds sourced in docs/SIM_FACTS.md item 14.
gaps.proposal: Pressure wire as a device in the PCI session using physiology.reading()/indices() with the rod-model sensor position (radiopacity transition visible), guide engagement state from the rod (wedge -> GUIDE_WEDGE coefficients), drift as an evolving offset, adenosine as an order with AV-block and symptom responses; pullback curves recorded as series; post-PCI re-measurement after stenting updates the lesion coefficients. Drive the injection model's coronary flow from the same flow() so angiographic transit and FFR are physically consistent.

gaps.gap: Procedure realism has no quantitative check against real cine statistics; only grey-level calibration and an expert-vs-novice score test exist.

The measurements in this report (contrast onset, plateau, early pedal release, global motion, angle fine-tuning, runs per study) were made with Pillow on datasets/library and can be repeated on rendered sim runs. VCSim3 reported face and content validation with 17 interventional radiologists (doi 10.1007/s11548-017-1679-1).
