audits.summary:
I audited the teaching and mentoring code and content (read-only), measured the content and the real-angiogram library myself, and read the simulation-education literature I cite below. The app has a lot of good material: 10 tracks, 68 modules, 231 lessons, 542 quiz items, 51 case studies, a seeded case generator that rates each case on engagement, RCA and view difficulty, and an SM-2 quiz scheduler. It also has several real assets for mentoring: an engagement and pressure state machine, a mistake ledger, a PCI event log and expert-labelled real cine runs. But the mentoring is shallow, and in places it undermines learning.

Main problems found:
1) Answers are shown on screen all the time, in every mode. The header chip and the 'Coach' box always show the true engagement state and its message. Labels, ostia, the valve plane and faint outlines of the vessels are on by default. The case traps are listed before the case starts. In the PCI lab, the QCA reference diameter and %DS appear after the first injection, and the recommended views are shown in bold. The SimMode 'exam' is defined but never used. 'Challenge — no hints' only turns off the H key.
2) Feedback runs constantly during the case and never fades. The literature I read says that, for novices, feedback at the end of a run transfers better than feedback during it (Walsh 2009; Hatala 2014).
3) There is no pre-brief, no time-out, no record of the procedure over time and no replay. Event times are stamped in fluoroscopy seconds, and training time is also recorded as fluoroscopy seconds.
4) Only 9 of the 24 MistakeCode values are ever raised by the simulator. View selection, excess contrast or fluoro, catheter choice and injecting without aspirating are never assessed, and requiredViews is not used in scoring.
5) Scoring targets are not tied to any validated benchmark. The app requires 4 diagnostic runs, a 75 mL contrast budget and 180 s of fluoro for a two-coronary study. The Jensen 2016 proficiency criterion is 8 cine loops, under 10 min, under 3 min of fluoro and under 50 mL. The app does not measure procedure time.
6) Progression is based on XP and case counts, not entrustment. The content itself teaches the EAPCI levels, but the code has none of it. recordExam is never called, and level 10 does not actually require the exam.
7) Spaced repetition covers only text quiz items. The mistake counts never decay, so once a weakness is flagged it stays a priority for good. The drills named in MISTAKE_INFO do not exist; their buttons just open a general section.
8) The PCI lab has no lesion assessment, sizing decision or heparin/ACT step done by the learner. Its debrief is a pass/fail checklist and nothing from it reaches the progress record.
9) The real-angiogram drills can be beaten by guessing the most common answer: always answering 'right dominant' scores 77.9%, always 'left coronary' 71.8%, and always 'normal' on the segment report 74.3%. There is also a scoring bug: for 36 of the 42 CADICA patients the 'most severe stenosis' answer can never be marked correct.
10) The quizzes and cases have a test-taking giveaway. Always picking the longest option scores 67.5% on the quiz. In the cases the best option is the uniquely longest in 86% of steps, and 0 of 257 steps actually branch.

Proposed mentor design (offline, no backend, no LLM). Build a new src/mentor/ layer with these parts:
- ProcedureRecorder: records the procedure state 10 times a second into typed arrays saved in IndexedDB, plus discrete events.
- metrics.ts: objective metrics based on the literature (procedure and fluoro time, cine runs, contrast, a dose index taken from the renderer's AEC, engagement attempts, aspiration and pressure-check compliance, view coverage, injection quality, an error score, and for PCI: lesion estimate error, sizing ratio and landing margins).
- MentorEngine: declarative rules, each with a five-step ladder of prompts (silent observation, question, cue, instruction, hard stop). How much it says fades with the learner's entrustment level. It also calls a time-out when the learner is stuck, can use offline speech synthesis, and in exam mode says nothing except safety stops.
- A pre-brief and time-out where the learner commits to a plan, which the debrief compares with what they actually did.
- A debrief built on PEARLS: the learner's reactions and self-rating, an annotated replay timeline that redraws the X-ray image at any moment, advocacy-inquiry 'what were you thinking' choices that lead to targeted teaching, and a summary that schedules practice.
- An EPA catalogue (ten Cate's eight sections) mapped to EAPCI levels I–V, with proficiency-based progression: minimum passing standards, zero critical errors in exam mode on unseen cases, and expiry if a skill is not practised.
- A case catalogue ordered from easy to hard within each EPA (Grover 2017).
- Spaced repetition of procedural errors: short scenarios that start at the moment of the error, graded on the measured outcome.
- Fixed and balanced real-image drills that add lesion localisation and confidence calibration.

All of these can be built on code that already exists (sceneBuilder is deterministic, plus caseGenerator presets, projection.ts, engagement.ts and pciGeom).

gaps.gap: The app shows the correct answer in every mode, so a learner never has to read the fluoroscopy or the pressure trace the way a real operator does. There is no exam mode, even though SimMode 'exam' is declared.
gaps.evidence: Simulator.tsx header StatusChip renders eng.kind ('Engaged', 'Near lm'), and the always-visible 'Coach' box renders eng.message (lines ~155, 238-243), including in Challenge.tsx (hideHints only disables the H key and hint button). useSimulatorStore.buildSim sets overlays {labels:true, ostia:true, valvePlane:true, transparent:true} for every mode, and FluoroView draws faint outlines of the vessel tree when transparent is on (line ~390). CoachPanel lists caseData.traps ('Watch out for'). AngioPci auto-reveals the QCA reference diameter, MLD and %DS after the first injection (setQca(true) line ~102), shows recommended views in bold (line ~178), and gives 'coach read-outs' of wire branch, mm from the ostium and device-to-lesion offset (lines ~275-283, 366-370). grep: SimMode 'exam' and 'tutorial-*' have 0 uses; recordExam has 0 callers.
gaps.proposal: Add src/mentor/visibility.ts: type AssessmentMode = 'guided'|'supervised'|'independent'|'exam'; interface VisibilityPolicy {stateChips:boolean; coachLine:boolean; overlays:Partial<Overlays>; traps:boolean; qca:'auto'|'after-estimate'|'off'; recommendedViews:boolean; wireReadout:boolean; hints:'free'|'costed'|'off'; mentor:'full'|'faded'|'safety-only'}. Each EPA's entrustment level picks the default policy. Exam = no chips, no coach line, all overlays off (and not toggleable), traps hidden, QCA only after the learner's own estimate, hints off, mentor limited to safety stops. Thread the policy through useSimulatorStore (store mode plus policy, and make loadCase(c,'exam') apply it), Simulator.tsx, CoachPanel.tsx, FluoroView.tsx, ControlPanel.tsx and AngioPci.tsx. Exam attempts call recordExam and feed entrustment (see the entrustment gap). Add unit tests that exam mode never renders eng.kind or eng.message.

gaps.gap: There is no mentor that speaks at the right moment, escalates or falls silent. Coaching is a constant stream: the engagement message updates continuously and the hint button returns one sentence. Nothing fades as the learner improves, there are no time-outs when stuck, and a dangerous action is never stopped before it happens.
gaps.evidence: buildHint() in useSimulatorStore.ts returns a single static string chosen from the engagement kind; the only cost of a hint is efficiency -2 (scoring.ts). The coach line always shows engagement.message. The PCI events list only reports outcomes after they happen. Walsh et al. 2009 (colonoscopy simulator, 30 novices): terminal feedback beat concurrent feedback on transfer, and the concurrent group's performance fell on transfer. Hatala et al. 2014 meta-analysis: feedback effect size 0.74, and terminal feedback appears more effective than concurrent feedback for novices' retention, which fits the guidance hypothesis.
gaps.proposal: New src/mentor/rules.ts and src/mentor/mentor.ts. interface MentorRule {id; epa:EpaId; phase:'access'|'engage'|'inject'|'views'|'wire'|'device'|'complication'; trigger:(ctx:MentorCtx)=>boolean; persistS:number; severity:'safety'|'technique'|'efficiency'; ladder:{L1q:string; L2cue:string; L3do:string; L4stop?:string}; cooldownS:number; frameOptions?:FrameOption[]} where MentorCtx = latest TelemetryFrame plus rolling windows (pushStreak, time in state, last aspirate, last pressure check, injections, cArm history). MentorEngine.step(ctx, policy) → MentorUtterance {t; ruleId; level:0..4; text; anchor:'pressure'|'fluoro'|'hub'|'cArm'; blocking:boolean}. Escalation: the starting step depends on entrustment level (L2-3: start at L1 question then go to L3 after a delay; L4: silent except safety; exam: L4 safety stop only, logged as a critical error, with the consequence allowed to play out in exam mode but blocked in guided mode). Time-out rule: no progress in engagement class for 60 s, or more than 3 catheter re-approaches, produces 'Pause. Talk me through your plan', with selectable plan frames. Example ladder for damped-before-inject: L1 'Before you inject — what is the pressure telling you?'; L2 'Look at the diastolic limb.'; L3 'That is ventricularised. Come back a millimetre until the trace recovers, then aspirate.'; L4 'Stop. Don't inject.' (fires when Space is pressed while isDeepDamp). Other starter rules: conus over-selection, LV entry, pushing against resistance (controls.resistance with a high pushStreak), injecting without a clean aspirate, a view that foreshortens the target segment, steep-angle dose while screening with no purpose, wire into a septal or diagonal branch, device advanced beyond the wire, balloon wider than 1.1× the local reference outside the lesion, stent deployed without an injection to confirm position. Every utterance goes into the telemetry for the debrief. Optional speech: speechSynthesis using only voices with localService===true, so it works offline; muted by default in exam mode. The existing teachingText strings can seed the L3 lines. Delays and cooldowns are tunable defaults, not values from the literature.

gaps.gap: Cases start straight away. The learner never commits to a plan (access route, first and backup catheter, planned views, contrast budget, anticipated difficulty), and there is no safety time-out. As a result the debrief cannot compare intent with what happened, and the content's own NatSSIPs material is never practised.
gaps.evidence: There is no pre-brief or time-out code in src/ui/sim, AngioPci.tsx or ProcedureLab.tsx (grep). Cases expose objectives, traps and recommendedCatheters, but only as display text. The content cites NatSSIPs 2 (refs.ts 'natssips2-2023') and teaches the logbook and consent (procedures-career.ts ~1148-1210). The PCI scenarios have rich briefs (angioPci.ts PCI_SCENARIOS) but no decision steps.
gaps.proposal: Add src/ui/mentor/PreBrief.tsx and interface ProcedurePlan {access:AccessRoute; catheters:{left:string; right:string; backup:string[]}; plannedViews:{left:string[]; right:string[]}; contrastBudgetMl:number; anticipated:string[]; heparinUnitsPerKg?:number (PCI); guide?:string; wire?:WireKind; strategy?:'direct-stent'|'predilate'|'prep-calcium'|'aspirate'}. The mentor asks 2-4 case-specific questions taken from a new content file src/content/mentor/prebriefs.ts (keyed by caseGenerator preset or PCI scenario id), with expected answers and the teaching for each. A time-out checklist component (patient and procedure, allergy or contrast reaction, renal function and contrast budget, anticoagulation, access site, devices available) must be completed before the beam turns on in supervised and exam modes. Store the plan on the attempt; debrief.ts scores plan quality and plan-to-execution adherence (for example, planned RAO caudal but never acquired it).

gaps.gap: The debrief is just 'dominant mistake + counts + positives' for the diagnostic sim and a pass/fail checklist for PCI. It has no timeline, no replay of the image at the moment of the error, no self-assessment and no structured reflection. Events are timestamped in fluoroscopy seconds, so everything that happens with the beam off shares one timestamp.
gaps.evidence: adaptiveCoach.coachCase picks the most frequent code. recompute() and inject() stamp events with t = round(s.fluoroTime,1) (useSimulatorStore.ts ~237, ~503), and finishCase calls addTrainingTime(Math.round(s.fluoroTime)). AngioPci debrief() returns items:{ok,text}[] and a score equal to the percentage of items passed. No replay or snapshot code exists (grep). PEARLS (Eppich & Cheng 2015) has reactions, description, analysis and summary phases. In analysis, directive feedback suits technical gaps where the reasoning is evident, and focused facilitation (advocacy-inquiry) suits cases where it is not. Rudolph et al. 2006: trainees' 'frames' drive their actions; advocacy (observation plus judgement) is paired with inquiry.
gaps.proposal: Add src/mentor/telemetry.ts: class ProcedureRecorder with columns as Float32Array at 10 Hz: tWall, tFluoro, cmdInsertion, insertion, cmdTorque, torque, wireInsertion, tipHeight, tipAz, depth, engKindIdx, pressKindIdx, sys, dia, laoRao, cranCaud, field, pulseRate, beamOn, cineOn, contrastMl, doseIdx, plus events: ProcEvent {tWall; kind:'inject'|'cine-start'|'cine-end'|'view'|'catheter'|'aspirate'|'pressure-check'|'hint'|'mentor'|'complication'|'device'|'inflate'; payload}. Persist through a 60-line IndexedDB wrapper (src/utils/idb.ts), keeping the last 50 attempts; about 20 columns × 6000 samples × 2 bytes after Int16 quantisation is roughly 240 kB per 10-minute case. Replace fluoroTime timestamps with tWall (keep tFluoro as a column). Add src/ui/mentor/ReplayTimeline.tsx with swimlanes (beam and cine bars, injections with mL, pressure-kind colour band, engagement-state band, C-arm angle trace, mentor prompts, errors as flags). Scrubbing redraws the X-ray frame by feeding the recorded state into buildXrayScene and XrayRenderer, which are deterministic given state, t and frame. Add src/mentor/debrief.ts following PEARLS: (1) Reactions: a 1-5 self-rating per EPA sub-skill plus an optional local text note. (2) Description: an auto-generated narrative of the timeline. (3) Analysis: choose up to 3 gaps by severity × recurrence. For gaps where the reasoning is evident (for example torque direction), use directive feedback with a replay clip. For decision gaps (for example injecting into a damped trace, or changing catheter too early), use advocacy-inquiry, e.g. 'I noticed you injected at 02:14 while the trace was ventricularised; I was worried about dissection. What were you seeing?'. The learner then picks a frame (FrameOption {id; text; teachingId}) such as 'I thought it was noise', 'I didn't look at the trace' or 'I thought aspiration was enough', and each frame unlocks targeted teaching and a drill. (4) Summary: the learner selects a take-home, and the system shows the metric table and schedules SkillCards (see the spaced-repetition gap). Show calibration: self-rating compared with the metric percentile.

gaps.gap: Most taught errors are never detected. View selection, injection quality, number of engagement attempts and procedure time are not measured, so these skills cannot be practised to a standard. The operator also cannot control how long to inject or film.
gaps.evidence: Of the 24 MistakeCode values, only 9 are ever raised (lv-entry, deep-engagement, lv-injection, damped-injection, non-selective-injection, air-embolism, dissection, too-much-pushing, vf-arrest). too-high, too-low, wrong-catheter, insufficient-withdrawal, wrong-rotation, over-rotation, non-coaxial, poor-view, vessel-misid, excess-fluoro, excess-contrast, ignored-pressure-warning, catheter-changed-early, catheter-changed-late and no-aspirate exist only in teachingText, adaptiveCoach and caseGenerator's MISTAKE_TO_PRESET, so curriculumEngine's adaptive drills for views, efficiency and catheter choice can never trigger. requiredViews is only used to set budgets (targetsFor) and to label cards in CaseLibrary. The diagnostic bolus lasts a fixed 4.8 s or 3.4 s (useSimulatorStore ~617) and PCI cine a fixed 4.2 s with injectDur 1.8 s. In my sample of real runs, 39 of 75 stopped filming while opacification was still at least 50% of peak, so cine length is an operator decision worth teaching. Jensen 2016 measured fluoro time, procedure time, cine loops, contrast, DAP, an error score and a performance score in real cases.
gaps.proposal: Add src/mentor/metrics.ts with interface DiagnosticMetrics {procTimeS; fluoroS; cineRuns; contrastMl; doseIdx; engageAttempts:{left; right}; timeToSelective:{left?; right?}; lvEntries; dampedEvents; injectWhileDamped; aspirateCompliance:number (fraction of injections preceded by a clean aspirate since the tip last moved); pressureCheckCompliance; catheterChanges:{early; late}; viewCoverage:{segment:AhaSegment; bestScore:number}[]; redundantRuns; injectionQuality:{runId; adequateFill:boolean; reflux:boolean; filmedToWashout:boolean; durationS}[]; errorScore; criticalErrors:string[]}. Definitions: an engagement attempt is an approach into a near- or coaxial-* state that ends in withdrawal to the sinus or ascending aorta without becoming selective. View coverage takes each acquired cine run's C-arm angles, projects every target AHA segment through projection.ts, and scores 1 − foreshortening × (1 + overlap with other opacified vessels). A segment is 'seen' when its score passes a threshold in at least one run, and poor-view is raised when a required segment is never seen. Use acceptance windows from real operators (measured: e.g. RCA LAO median LAO 26 [IQR 23–30]) rather than exact preset matching. Injection quality: require pre-contrast frames, a hand-injection duration (hold Space to inject, release to stop) long enough to fill the vessel, and filming for at least 2 cardiac cycles after peak (or until collaterals fill in CTO cases). Raise all 15 missing codes from these metrics (e.g. no-aspirate when an injection had no clean aspirate in a safe position; excess-contrast and excess-fluoro against the plan budget; catheter-changed-early when the change comes before 2 attempts). Dose index: the renderer's AEC already computes N0 = uCounts/Tref (XrayRenderer.ts ~335). Expose Tref through a 1-pixel readback every 0.5 s (or compute it on the CPU from the same 5 metering points) and accumulate doseIdx += (uCounts/Tref) × fieldArea × pulses. Report it in relative units against a reference AP frame. This replaces VitalsMonitor's dap = fluoroTime × 18 (line ~136) and makes collimation, pulse rate and steep angles teachable, without claiming absolute Gy·cm².

gaps.gap: Pass/fail and scores rest on arbitrary weights and budgets, not on any proficiency benchmark. Procedure time is not measured, and the targets are lenient compared with the one benchmark I found in the literature.
gaps.evidence: scoring.ts: safety penalties of 12/6/22/4/45/30/40, a final score of 0.4·safety + 0.28·efficiency + 0.32·anatomy, and casePassed at a final score of 65 or more. targetsFor gives requiredDiagnostic 4, contrastBudget 75 mL and fluoroBudget 180 s for both coronaries (2 runs, 40 mL and 120 s otherwise). Jensen 2016 (EuroIntervention RCT) required a complete CA with 'eight standardised cine loops in less than ten minutes, fluoroscopy time less than three minutes and using less than 50 ml of contrast', and VR-trained beginners then had lower real fluoro time (558 vs 842 s), procedure time (1356 vs 1623 s) and error score (15 vs 27). My library measurement: median runs per study were CADICA 8, AngioCAD 6, CoronaryDominance 5–6, and real studies acquired a median of 4 distinct LCA standard views. Proficiency-based progression to a predefined target in cardiac device implantation gave 61.2% fewer critical errors (Mascheroni 2024).
gaps.proposal: Add src/mentor/standards.ts: interface PassingStandard {epa; metric:keyof Metrics; op:'<='|'>='|'=='; value:number; source:'jensen-2016'|'local-expert'|'app-default'; critical?:boolean}. Default diagnostic full study: criticalErrors == 0, cineRuns of at least 8 standardised loops with every required segment seen, procTimeS <= 600, fluoroS <= 180, contrastMl <= 50 (all labelled source 'jensen-2016'). Add an 'Expert calibration' mode in which a trainer runs the benchmark cases. Their metrics are saved as a local JSON benchmark (export and import via the existing exportJSON pattern), and the passing standard for this simulator becomes the expert mean or limit, as proficiency-based progression requires. Keep a composite score only as formative information; progression decisions use the per-metric standards. Show the source of each threshold in the UI.

gaps.gap: Progression works like a game: XP, streaks, levels earned by case count and average safety, and a '10 h/day' intensity option. The content teaches EAPCI competence levels and entrustment, but none of it is implemented. There are no EPAs, no summative entrustment, no expiry, and exams are never recorded.
gaps.evidence: useProgressStore.computeLevel uses only casesCompleted and the safety average of the last 20 attempts. LEVELS (curriculum.ts) runs from 'Aortic Root Novice' to 'CathMaster' at 220 cases with safety of at least 90, and level 10's 'pass Master Assessment' is never checked. recordExam has 0 callers. Dashboard shows XP. INTENSITY_MINUTES.obsessive = 600. Stage in schema.ts 'loosely mirrors entrustment' but is only a label. procedures-career.ts teaches 'stages of entrustment' and EAPCI. EAPCI 2020 defines competence levels I–V; for example, Level IV is first operator 'without the direct supervision of a senior IC operator', and the curriculum recommends no minimum case volumes. ten Cate & Taylor 2021 (AMEE Guide 140) set out eight EPA description sections, including information sources for summative entrustment and the time to expiry if not practised. Supervision scales run from 'observe only' to 'execute independently' (Weiss 2021). Distributed practice beat massed practice on retention and transfer (Moulton 2006).
gaps.proposal: Add src/mentor/competency.ts: type EpaId = 'access-radial'|'access-femoral'|'lca-engage'|'rca-engage'|'diag-study'|'diag-report'|'lesion-assess'|'pci-simple'|'pci-calcium'|'pci-stemi'|'pci-cto'|'complication-bailout'. interface EpaDef {id; title; specification; limitations; risks; competencies:string[]; prerequisites:EpaId[]; evidence:{metricStandards:PassingStandard[]; examPassesRequired:number; distinctCases:boolean; minDaysSpread:number}; expiryDays:number}. interface EntrustmentRecord {epa; level:1|2|3|4|5 (mapped to EAPCI I–V and the supervision scale); evidence:{attemptId; mode; passed; date}[]; awardedAt?; expiresAt?}. Rules: a level is awarded only after N exam-mode passes on distinct unseen generated cases, spread over at least 2 days, with zero critical errors. Level 2→3 needs supervised-mode passes; 3→4 needs exam passes. Expiry drops the level by one and schedules a refresher. The level drives VisibilityPolicy and mentor fading. Replace XP, streak and 'CathMaster' copy with a simulator logbook (attempt, role, case features, metrics, outcome) that mirrors the logbook lesson. Remove or relabel the 'obsessive' intensity, and cap blocked practice per EPA per day in curriculumEngine so practice is spread out. Add a progress migration in hydrate().

gaps.gap: Cases are reached by preset or at random, and the daily challenge is random at difficulty 3 or above. There is no ladder from easy to hard within a competency and no 'master this rung before moving on' gate.
gaps.evidence: Challenge.tsx calls generateRandomCase(seed,{minDifficulty:3}). CaseLibrary.tsx groups cases by PRESET_ORDER and shows caseDifficultyAxes (engagement, rca, view), but nothing gates or sequences them. Grover et al. 2017 RCT (37 novice endoscopists): a curriculum that 'progressed in complexity and difficulty' beat the same 6 hours with cases in random order of difficulty on the first two clinical colonoscopies.
gaps.proposal: Add src/content/mentor/catalogue.ts: interface CatalogueEntry {id; source:{kind:'preset'; preset:string; seed:string}|{kind:'pci'; scenario:string}|{kind:'real'; runIds:string[]}; epa:EpaId; competencies:string[]; rung:1..6; axes:{engagement; rca; view}; exam:boolean; teachingFocus:string}. Build a ladder per EPA from generateBatch(preset, seed, n) sorted by caseDifficultyAxes. The learner must meet the passing standard twice on a rung before the next rung unlocks. Exam cases are a held-out pool of seeds never used in practice. Once a rung is mastered, mix cases from mastered rungs together for retention. CaseLibrary and DailyPlan read the ladder state. Daily challenge = the next rung of the weakest due EPA.

gaps.area: Spaced repetition linked to procedural errors
gaps.gap: Spaced repetition covers only text quiz items. Procedural errors pile up in a ledger that never decays. The remedial drills named in MISTAKE_INFO do not exist; their buttons just open a general section such as the free lab.
gaps.evidence: srs.ts review() is called only from answerQuiz. ProgressProfile.spacedRepetition / SrsItem is declared but never written. useProgressStore.addMistakes only increments counts, and curriculumEngine.adaptiveInserts uses fixed cumulative thresholds (for example lv-entry plus lv-injection of 3 or more), so a priority stays on permanently. MISTAKE_INFO names drills such as 'Recover-from-LV-entry drill', 'Torque-direction drill' and 'Aspirate-before-inject drill' that appear nowhere else in src (grep). Each drillSection opens 'free', 'pressure-trainer' and so on.
gaps.proposal: Add src/mentor/skillCards.ts: interface SkillCard {id:`${EpaId}:${MistakeCode}`; memory:QuizMemory (reuse srs.ts); scenario:{preset:string; seedBase:string; startState:Partial<ControlState>&{catheterId?; cArm?; wire?}}; passRule:PassingStandard[]}. Each card is a 1-3 minute micro-scenario that starts at the moment of the error, for example the tip already in the conus, a ventricularised RCA, a wire in S1, or an oversized balloon loaded. Pass or fail is decided from the measured metrics, not by self-report, and fed into review(). Cards are created from debrief gaps. dueIds() includes cards, and the Review section shows both quiz items and skill cards. Weight the ledger with exponential decay (weight = Σ exp(−Δdays/14)) for adaptiveInserts and weakestSkillPreset. Implement each named MISTAKE_INFO drill as a SkillCard template, so the 'Drill' button launches the real scenario.

gaps.gap: In the PCI lab the learner never has to assess the lesion or justify device sizing; the reference diameter and %DS are handed over. There is no heparin/ACT, guide-support or strategy decision. The debrief is a binary checklist, and nothing reaches the progress, mistake or entrustment records. View selection and foreshortening are not assessed, and contrast per injection is fixed.
gaps.evidence: AngioPci.tsx shows 'QCA: reference … MLD … DS … length' as soon as the first injection is given. finish() calls only recordSim(`pci-${id}`, score), which keeps only the best score and run count. angioPci.inject() always adds 8 or 6 mL. debrief() checks stent coverage, residual stenosis, a 1.5 mm margin, a stent-to-reference ratio between 0.95 and 1.25, calcium prep, dissection, perforation, flow, contrast and fluoro, with the score equal to the percentage passed and caps for perforation and for no stent. Only 4 scenarios exist. moveWire logs side-branch entries but does not count them.
gaps.proposal: Add a 'Lesion assessment' step: on a frozen end-diastolic cine frame the learner places calipers (reference proximal and distal, MLD, length). Score the absolute error against g.lesion.refDiameter, the computed MLD and s.target.lengthMm, and reveal QCA only afterwards (policy.qca = 'after-estimate'). Add a sizing rationale (choose a reference basis: distal reference, mean reference, or imaging) and an ACT/heparin step with simulated ACT, with the mentor stopping device advance if the ACT was never checked in supervised mode. PciMetrics: {procTimeS; fluoroS; contrastMl (from injection hold time × syringe rate); cineRuns; wireTimeS; sideBranchEntries; distalTipExcursions; workingViewForeshortening; lesionEstimateErrorMm; sizingRatio; landingMarginMm:{prox; dist}; predilated; postdilatedInStent; residualDS; complications[]; timeToRecogniseComplication; correctBailout:boolean}. Add PCI rules to the MentorEngine (wire in a septal branch, tip moving too far distally, device beyond the wire, an oversized balloon outside the stent, stent deployed without a positioning injection, perforation needing recognition and a balloon to seal within a set time). Record a PciAttempt with telemetry and a debrief. Move PCI_SCENARIOS into the catalogue and generate variants (vessel, position, length, calcium) from caseGenerator for the ladder. Add SimId 'angio-pci' so pci-core and pci-complex modules can send learners here.

gaps.gap: Learners can score well by always giving the most common answer. One patient-case question cannot be answered correctly for most patients. Some projection labels are ambiguous. Items are drawn at random with no spaced repetition, there is no localisation task even though expert boxes exist, there is no confidence calibration, and the Academy does not link to these drills.
gaps.evidence: Measured: the dominance drill pool is 643 patients, 501 right-dominant, so always 'Right' scores 77.9%. The artery drill has 3360 LCA and 1319 RCA runs, so always 'LCA' scores 71.8%. In the AngioCAD segment report 4592 of 6180 segments are NL, so always 'normal' scores 74.3%. For the CADICA patient case, DEGREE_OPTIONS (RealAngiograms.tsx ~219) do not match the dataset's labels '>70%', '> 70%' and '20-50%' after normalise(), so only 6 of 42 patients can be scored correct. 564 of 1625 CoronaryDominance runs (34.7%) lie within 5° of a standardView() boundary. makeItems uses Math.random shuffle and recordSim stores only the best score. SimId has no 'angio-real' (schema.ts), so modules cannot route learners to the drills.
gaps.proposal: In RealAngiograms.tsx, (a) sample items stratified by class (equal positives and negatives per set) and report balanced accuracy and Cohen's kappa against the expert label rather than raw percentage. (b) Use each dataset's own classes per question: for CADICA maxDegree, options <20% / 20–50% / >70% (fix normalise for '> 70%'). (c) For the projection drill, drop runs within 5° of a boundary or accept either neighbour, and give the recorded angles as feedback. (d) Add 'Locate the worst lesion': on a CADICA keyframe the learner clicks, and it is a hit if inside the expert box with a 10% margin. Pair it with grading so detection and grading are scored separately. (e) Add a confidence slider per answer and track a Brier score plus per-learner over- or under-calling bias for stenosis grade (signed category error). (f) Make each run id a QuizMemory item so wrong reads come back. (g) Add SimId 'angio-real' with a drill parameter so diagnostic modules embed specific drills. (h) Save drill attempts with per-item results for learning curves. Keep the dataset attribution as it is.

gaps.area: Item quality of quizzes and branching cases
gaps.gap: The quizzes and cases give away the answer through option length, and the cases described as branching never branch. Wrong choices are explained but their consequences never play out.
gaps.evidence: Measured with an esbuild bundle of src/content plus a node script: across 542 quiz items the correct option is the uniquely longest in 352 (64.9%), and an 'always pick the longest' strategy scores 67.5% (84.6% on difficulty-3 items). The median ratio of correct-option length to mean distractor length is 1.67. In the 51 cases the best option is the uniquely longest in 221 of 257 steps (86.0%), there are 3.58 options per step, and 0 of 257 steps use a non-sequential next. CasePlayer.tsx's header says 'Branching case player'. Answer-position bias is already handled by shuffling, except for 15 positional items.
gaps.proposal: Extend src/content/validate.ts and content.test.ts with a length-cue rule: fail if the correct option is longer than 1.3× the mean distractor length, or is uniquely longest, in more than 35% of a module's items (a tunable project rule). Rewrite the flagged distractors to the same length and form. Give cases consequence steps: CaseOption.next pointing to complication or recovery steps when a non-best option is chosen, and a 'stateDelta' (contrastMl, haemodynamics) so poor choices compound. Store item analytics locally (p-value, and point-biserial correlation against module mastery) and surface weak items in a dev panel. Add image-based items that use the real-angiogram library (CinePlayer block kind 'cine' in schema.ts Block) so knowledge checks include real images.

gaps.gap: Module 'mastery' measures only reading and the last quiz answer. A learner can reach 100% on a PCI module without ever performing the skill. The Academy cannot send learners to the X-ray cath-lab PCI or the real-angiogram drills.
gaps.evidence: srs.moduleMastery = 0.5 × lessons read + 0.5 × quiz items whose last answer was correct (srs.ts ~74-83). mastery.tsx trackMastery averages these. SimId (schema.ts) lacks 'angio-pci' and 'angio-real', and grep finds 0 references to these sections in any track. The 76 sim blocks point to 'free', 'pci-bench' and similar via SIM_SECTION, with no completion criterion.
gaps.proposal: Give Module an optional 'evidence' field: {epa:EpaId; standardIds:string[]}[]. Compute mastery as a weighted sum of knowledge (quiz memory with reps of 2 or more, not just the last answer), skill (passes against the passing standard on linked EPA rungs) and image reading (balanced accuracy on linked real drills). Show the three parts separately in Pathway. Add SimId 'angio-pci' and 'angio-real' (with scenario or drill parameters) to SIM_SECTION, and replace the free-text sim block 'task' with a structured task that has a pass rule, so completion is recorded.

gaps.gap: When a learner is stuck, the mentor cannot demonstrate. There is no model of expert hand movements, and no way to compare the learner's catheter manipulation with an expert's (path length, torque reversals).
gaps.evidence: There is no demonstrator or expert-trajectory code. The engagement dynamics (engagement.ts, stepDynamics) can be run as a forward model, and CatheterHub already shows commanded and actual hub positions. Jensen 2016 counted handling errors in its error score, and the literature summary McGaghie et al. 2021 cites hand-movement counts as an expert-performance measure.
gaps.proposal: Add src/mentor/demonstrator.ts: a short-horizon model-predictive search over discrete hub actions {advance, withdraw, torque ±fine, relax, wire ±} using computeTip, computeEngagement and stepDynamics as the forward model. Cost: height error to the sinus or ostium, azimuth error to the target ostium, a penalty on deep or LV states, and a penalty on push against resistance. From the current state it returns an action sequence to selective, coaxial engagement. 'Show me' plays the plan as a ghost hub with timed key prompts, then hands control back (counted as a hint at the current entrustment level). Also record trainer runs in Expert calibration mode as reference trajectories and compute economy-of-motion metrics (total |Δinsertion|, total |Δtorque|, torque reversals, time to coaxial) against them in the debrief.

gaps.gap: The learner is never asked to rate themselves or reflect, so how well their self-assessment matches reality is never trained, even though PEARLS starts from the learner's own self-assessment.
gaps.evidence: There is no self-rating or reflection field in ProgressProfile, CaseAttempt or any debrief component. PEARLS (Eppich & Cheng 2015) includes learner self-assessment (e.g. plus-delta) as one of its three strategies and a learner-guided summary phase. McGaghie et al. 2021 list trainees monitoring their own strategies, errors and understanding as a component of deliberate practice.
gaps.proposal: Before the debrief, ask for 1-5 ratings on 4-6 EPA sub-skills plus a plus/delta note (stored locally in the attempt). After the metrics are shown, display a calibration plot (self-rating compared with the metric-based percentile across the learner's own history) and flag consistent overconfidence on safety items. The summary phase requires the learner to pick or write one 'next time I will…' line, which the mentor repeats in the next case's pre-brief.

audits.summary:
I benchmarked CathMaster against academic and commercial cath-lab simulators and against what the Philips Azurion coronary suite offers in clinical use. I also took 14 sets of real measurements comparing the renderer and the procedure engines with the openly licensed cine library. No project files were modified. Scratch scripts are in /private/tmp/claude-502/cathmaster-research/ (m1_angles.py through m8_population.py, plus ts/simMotion.ts). Simulator frames were captured in a separate background tab of the dev server that was already running, using the existing window.__pciDraw dev hook, and the tab was then closed.

What the state of the art offers:
- Imperial SimCath is a commercial prototype of a simulated cath lab: a Unity port, a multi-port haptic interface and a motorised mock C-arm. Its group's VCSim3 models catheters and wires as inextensible Cosserat rods tuned against CT-scanned real instruments, and adds contrast flow, cardiac motion, balloons and stents.
- Mentice (Coronary Essentials, VIST Virtual Patient, Case-It) adds FFR/RFR, femoral and radial access, complications that respond to vital signs, expert benchmarking, CT/MR import for patient-specific rehearsal, and integration with real C-arms.
- Surgical Science ANGIO Mentor adds haptics, PROcedure Rehearsal Studio, a drug panel with vitals, team training, and CTO and bifurcation modules.
- Philips (sales pages and the ClarityIQ white paper) offers:
  - Motion-compensated temporal noise reduction, adaptive spatial noise reduction that preserves wires, and multi-band harmonisation and enhancement.
  - Copper filtration of 0.1 to 0.4 mm, three fluoro flavours (stated cardiac fluoro dose rates 0.2 to 0.9 mGy/s), and higher air kerma when smaller detector fields are used.
  - Dynamic Coronary Roadmap: in the DCR4Contrast trial of 356 patients, contrast was 64.6 vs 90.8 mL and cine runs 8.7 vs 11.7.
  - StentBoost: averages frames registered on the two balloon markers to show the stent.
  - iFR and IVUS co-registration: pullback under continuous fluoro at 15 pulses/s optimal, 7.5 minimum.

Evidence on transfer to real performance:
- Simulation transfers: the Chaer randomised trial and the Popovic 2019 trial in coronary angiography, which reported shorter procedure time and lower dose in real cases.
- Simulation-based education with deliberate practice had an effect size of 0.71 against traditional clinical training (McGaghie).
- Proficiency-based progression reduced errors by 60% and time by 15% across 12 randomised studies (Mazzone).
- Spaced practice improves retention.
- Fidelity alone adds only 1 to 2% (Norman). Feedback and mastery learning are what drive learning.
- A 2026 review names the barriers as weak haptics, limited validation and cost.

"Beyond the state of the art" for a browser-only laptop simulator therefore means seven things:
1. Fluoroscopy whose statistics are measured and fitted against thousands of real cines, with a blinded real-vs-simulated test built in.
2. Devices that are physical rods, not state machines.
3. A whole-patient haemodynamic model reacting to every action.
4. Patients drawn from measured population variability, including real CTA trees.
5. Physiology, IVUS and dose physics inside the same image.
6. A proficiency-based mentor with expert benchmarks and spaced practice.
7. Reading training at scale on thousands of real runs with expert labels.

What the code already has:
- An exact-interval WebGL2 renderer with AEC, Poisson noise, dynamic range compression, a recursive filter, collaterals and blush.
- A 4,718-run real library with six reading drills.
- A tip-spring catheter dynamics model in `engagement.ts`.
- A 1D topology wire for PCI in `angioPci.ts`.
- Separate engines for haemodynamics, pressure wire, IVUS/OCT, IABP and MCS that are not coupled to the cath-lab PCI.
- Rule-based end-of-case coaching in `adaptiveCoach.ts`.
- A haptics abstraction with only a WebHID stub.

What the measurements found:
- **Opacified area is about 3 to 4 times too small.** The simulator's area darker by more than 10 grey levels at peak is 5.6 to 6.9% of the field, against a real median of 22.5%.
- **Grey levels vary with the view.** Real Philips frames have a nearly constant 5th percentile of 93 to 98 across views; the simulator's ranges from 74 to 131, and LAO views are 20 to 33 levels too light.
- **Heart motion is too abrupt.** The 95th percentile of motion speed is 7.6 to 15.2 px/frame in the simulator against 6.2 in real cines, because the contraction envelope is zero for 47% of the cycle. The cardiac silhouette does not beat at all.
- **Noise is weaker and more correlated than Philips.** After matching JPEG compression the simulator gives sigma 1.7 to 2.7 with lag-1 correlation about 0.37, against sigma 4.6 and lag-1 0.16 in the Philips set. Across vendors, real noise ranges from 0.8 to 7.5.
- **Every patient has the same body.** Body habitus, heart size and heart orientation are fixed, so only the coronary template varies between cases.
- **PCI controls are discrete steps.** The wire moves in 2 or 5 mm buttons and 20° torque clicks.
- **No dose is computed.** There is no air kerma, dose-area product, skin dose or operator dose.

gaps.gap: There is no automated sim-versus-real realism metric and no blinded discrimination test, so there is no way to show that 'looks fake' has been fixed. The display chain was calibrated once against grey-level quartiles only.
gaps.evidence: The image chain in src/render/xray/sceneBuilder.ts is fitted by hand (drc 0.7, level -0.12). My comparison using identical metrics on library frames and on frames from the window.__pciDraw dev hook exposed four independent mismatches: grey-level percentiles by view, opacified area, noise texture and motion speed (see measurements). None of these is tracked by tests. The rationale is Norman 2012 (high and low fidelity differ by only 1-2% in transfer unless realism is purposeful) and Ilgen/Cook 2013 (feedback, mastery learning and higher fidelity associated with better outcomes): realism has to be measured.
gaps.proposal: Add scripts/angio_library/realism_metrics.py (PIL + stdlib, reusing the m2-m7 methods). Per dataset and view family it computes: grey percentiles p1/p5/p50/p95; sigma-clipped residual noise against a Gaussian blur (sigma 1.2) with lag-1 and lag-2 autocorrelation; time-density curve D(t) = mean(max(0, B - I_t)) with B the lightest of the first 3 frames, giving rise, peak and half-duration; opacified area fraction >10 and >20 levels at peak; patch-tracked motion as peak-to-peak and P95 frame-to-frame speed; and heart rate from autocorrelation of the frame-difference signal. Output goes to datasets/library/realism_targets.json. Add a dev-only hook window.__xrayDump(n, bolusT[]) in FluoroView.tsx and AngioPci.tsx that returns the same statistics computed in-page (port of the JS used here), plus a Vitest 'realism budget' test that runs the scene builder headless for the geometric and temporal metrics. In RealAngiograms.tsx add a two-alternative forced-choice drill: a real clip and a simulated clip at the same C-arm angles (taken from the index.json angles), the user picks the real one, and the percentage correct is logged. The target is about 50%, meaning indistinguishable. This turns 'make it 10000% realistic' into a measurable target.

gaps.gap: The display stage is a single-scale DRC with a fixed level, a single unsharp mask and a recursive filter without motion compensation. Real cardiac systems produce a nearly view-invariant grey distribution through harmonisation and auto-windowing, and filter moving vessels with motion-compensated temporal noise reduction.
gaps.evidence: Real Philips frames (25 runs per family, mid-run frame) have p5/p50/p95 of 94/139/219 (LCA RAO-CRA), 93/132/196 (RAO-CAU), 98/136/197 (LAO-CRA), 98/145/211 (LAO-CAU), 95/129/201 (AP-CRA) and 93/140/197 (RCA LAO), so p5 sits in 93-98 for every view. Simulator at 25 cm field, bolus t = 2 s: RAO20/CRA24 74/141/185, RAO22/CAU22 84/144/189, LAO32/CRA26 129/159/209, LAO42/CAU28 131/152/198, AP/CRA30 97/130/220. Its p5 spans 74-131 and the LAO views are 20-33 levels too light. The ClarityIQ white paper (philips.com.co whitepaper-clarity-iq.PDF, pp. 6-9) describes: temporal noise reduction (SNR about sqrt(n) frames) with motion compensation that aligns moving structures before averaging; spatial noise reduction over larger neighbourhoods that preserves vessels and guidewires; frequency-band enhancement that boosts high and attenuates low frequencies ('harmonization'); and parameters tuned per application. DISPLAY_FS in XrayRenderer.ts uses fixed textureLod levels 0.85, 2.2, 5.2 and 5.5 and mixes the previous frame without alignment.
gaps.proposal:
Replace DISPLAY_FS with a generic multi-pass chain. These are published image-processing principles, not a copy of any vendor's algorithm.
(1) Build a Laplacian pyramid from the existing trans mip chain (levels 0-6) in log space and apply per-band gains: harmonisation attenuates bands 4-6, edge enhancement boosts bands 1-2, and noise coring soft-thresholds band 0-1 coefficients below k * sigma_noise, which is known from the photon count.
(2) Auto-window: render mip level 4 (48x48 at 768) into a 64-bin histogram target with additive blending (a vertex shader scatters points into bins), read it back one frame late, as a real AEC does, to avoid a GPU stall, and set window and level so that p5, p50 and p95 hit the per-profile targets from realism_targets.json.
(3) Motion-compensated temporal filter: the scene builder knows the true projected motion, so pass a coarse 16x16 motion field (projected displacement of the heart-surface samples between frames) and sample uPrev at uv - motion. Where motion is not modelled, fall back to block matching on mip 3.
(4) Add 'processing profiles' (for example 'flat panel, low noise' fitted to the CADICA statistics and 'flat panel, cardiac' fitted to the CoronaryDominance statistics) as parameter sets in sceneBuilder.ts.
Cost stays at a few full-screen passes at 768 px, well within 15 frames/s.

gaps.area: Iodine, contrast mixing and opacified territory
gaps.gap: Simulated injections opacify about a quarter of the field area that real injections do, and contrast transport is a smoothstep front at a constant 115 mm/s with one fixed concentration. There is no mixing with coronary flow, no streaming in an under-filled vessel, no reflux related to injection rate in the PCI lab, and too few small branches.
gaps.evidence: Opacified area (pixels darkened by more than 10 grey levels at peak, at 128 px, central 76%): real CoronaryDominance median 22.5% (IQR 16.2-34.1%, n = 60; frame-3 baseline 6.0%), dominance-main 18.2%, CADICA 23.7%. Area darkened by more than 20 levels: 10.9% vs simulator 3.2-4.5%. Mean darkening peak D: real 7.34 (IQR 5.51-10.88) vs simulator 1.85-2.55 in six views at 20 cm (area >10 levels 5.6-6.9%; 3.8% at 25 cm). Darkening inside opacified pixels is similar (real 20, simulator 25 levels), so the gap is territory, not iodine density. Time-density: real Philips median rise (10 to 90%) 1.37 s, peak at 1.93 s, at least 50% of peak for 2.8 s (n = 90); CADICA 2.1/2.75/3.9 s. Simulator in RAO CRA peaks at 1.4 s with about 2.0 s above half its excess, because injectDur is fixed at 1.8 s in AngioPci.tsx. Code: sceneBuilder.ts sets conc = 350*(0.55+0.35*peak)*smooth(...); PCI passes plume 'none'; coronaryTree.ts adds 7-24 twigs per host with r0 at or above 0.17 mm. The upgrade roadmap already lists 'streaming/incomplete opacification' and an 'injection-force model' as missing.
gaps.proposal:
(1) Injection as a continuous control: drag or trigger depth sets the syringe flow Q_inj in mL/s, logged as contrast volume.
(2) Run 1D advection-dispersion on the vessel graph (each TreeVessel already has pathMm and a parent index). Concentration at the ostium is c0 = 350 * Q_inj / max(Q_inj, Q_cor), where Q_cor comes from physiology.ts resistances() with the case lesions and the phasic flow pattern. When Q_inj < Q_cor, contrast streams (incomplete, layered opacification, rendered by reducing the effective radius of the iodine ribbon). When Q_inj > Q_cor, the excess refluxes into the sinus and root plume (existing BonePrim code) and the cusp opacifies. Dispersion uses a Taylor-dispersion coefficient per vessel. About 3,000 samples per frame on the CPU is cheap.
(3) Grow the distal tree by constrained constructive optimisation (CCO) or Murray-law branching on the heart surface down to about 0.15 mm radius, with territory filling per artery, so that the area statistic approaches the real 16-34%.
(4) Fit vessel radii, branch density and Q_inj defaults so that the area, peak D and time-density targets from realism_targets.json are met per view.

gaps.gap: The catheter is not a physical object. The tip sits on a circle around the root axis, with azimuth taken from 'torque' and height from 'insertion'. The body is a fixed aortic polyline plus a preformed Hermite curve. Engagement comes from distance and alignment thresholds per difficulty level, and wind-up, whip and prolapse are spring heuristics. In the diagnostic view the 0.035 wire is drawn as a straight two-point segment from the tip.
gaps.evidence: engagement.ts: computeTip() returns pos = (0, seatHeight - insertion, 0) + radial(az) * min(reach, sinusRadius + 1.5); THRESH holds selDist 7/5/3.6 and alignSel 0.85/0.9/0.94 by difficulty; prolapse is 'c.insertion += 3.2' when forwardPressure > 3.2 - bias. thorax.ts aorticCourse() is a fixed point list per route. FluoroView.tsx passes wire pts [tip.pos, tip.pos + dir * wireLen]. Literature: VCSim3 (Imperial, the SimCath group) uses an inextensible Cosserat rod with properties optimised against CT-scanned real instruments (doi 10.1007/s11548-017-1679-1). Kirchhoff-rod guidewire models run in real time at 30 fps or more (doi 10.1007/s11548-017-1583-8, 10.1016/j.compmedimag.2014.08.002). The Sharei 2018 review compares FEM, mass-spring and rigid multibody models (doi 10.1117/1.JMI.5.1.010902). The project roadmap itself lists 'catheter and wire as discrete elastic rods' as still to do.
gaps.proposal: Add src/simulation/rod/ with a position-based discrete Cosserat rod: nodes plus quaternion frames, stretch/shear, bend/twist constraints, and an XPBD solver with about 10 iterations per substep at 240 Hz in a Web Worker. Use about 100 nodes at 5 mm for the shaft and 40 nodes at 1.5 mm distally. Each catheter in data/catheters.ts gets a rest-curvature profile (primary and secondary curves) and bending and torsional stiffness, with the stiffness values sourced, not guessed. Model the vessels as a swept-tube signed-distance field: centreline plus radius for the femoral/iliac/aorta/arch/subclavian/radial routes (extend aorticCourse to 3D tubes) and the sinus of Valsalva as three ellipsoidal bulges whose ostia come from anatomy.ts. Collision uses closest point on the tube centreline, with Coulomb friction along the tangent, so torque transmission, wind-up, whip, deep seating, backup force against the opposite wall and prolapse all emerge. The hub boundary condition comes from the existing cmdInsertion/cmdTorque. Replace computeTip() and computeEngagement() thresholds with geometric predicates on the rod: tip inside the ostium tube, coaxiality from the dot product of tip tangent and ostium axis, depth along the vessel, and wall contact force from the constraint impulses, which also feed the damped/ventricularised pressure in pressure.ts. The rendered catheter (sceneBuilder catheterRoot) becomes the rod itself, and the 0.035 wire becomes a second, coaxial rod. Expected CPU cost is well under 2 ms per frame for about 300 nodes (an estimate to be confirmed by profiling).

gaps.gap: PCI wiring is a 1D walk along the branch list. A side branch is entered when cos(tipAngle - takeOffAngle) > 0.6. Inputs are buttons and keys in steps of 2 or 5 mm and 20° of torque. There is no wire curvature inside the vessel, no tip prolapse or J-loop, no whipping, no vessel straightening and no guide back-out when devices are pushed. The wire is drawn along the vessel centreline.
gaps.evidence: angioPci.ts moveWire() uses branch entry 'if (Math.cos(st.tipAngle - beta) > 0.6)'; canCross() is a rule on wire type; torqueWire adds dRad. AngioPci.tsx keyboard: w/s = ±2 mm, q/e = ±π/9; buttons ◂5, ◂2, 2▸, 5▸ and ⟲/⟳. The user says 'the procedure feels like a game'. Skalidis 2026 names the absence of robust haptic feedback as a principal barrier of VR PCI simulation (doi 10.1007/s10554-026-03782-x).
gaps.proposal: Simulate the 0.014 wire as a second Cosserat rod living in heart-surface coordinates, so that it beats with the heart. Lumen constraint is the TreeVessel radius at each sample, using the existing samplePos and per-frame contraction. The tip segment has a user-shaped bend (angle and length set in a 'shape the wire' step) and a stiffness gradient per wire kind (workhorse, polymer, CTO), with values taken from manufacturer specifications. Branch selection, prolapse into a J when pushed against a wall, deep tip deflection into septals, and wire bias in tortuous segments then emerge. Devices (balloon, stent, IVUS) ride the rod. Pushing a device adds axial load at the guide tip, which feeds the catheter rod from the previous gap, so the guide backs out unless it has support (deep seating or a buddy wire). Continuous input: mouse drag or trackpad for push/pull, horizontal drag or wheel for torque through a virtual torquer with lag, and fine mode on Shift (as CatheterHub.tsx already does for the diagnostic catheter). Keep the existing event log and teaching messages, but trigger them from rod-geometry events.

gaps.area: Whole-patient haemodynamics coupled to every action
gaps.gap: The PCI cath lab has no ECG, pressure or vital-sign coupling at all. Rich engines exist (lumped circulation, pressure morphologies, ECG with ST shifts, pericardiocentesis) but they live in separate labs.
gaps.evidence: A grep of src/ui/sections/AngioPci.tsx for ecg|pressure|Vitals|ischaem returns nothing. angioPci.ts PciState has no haemodynamic fields. Slow flow, perforation and dissection are booleans that only write log text. circulation.ts exports step(), activation() and pressures() (time-varying elastance); ecg.ts produces ST deviation; pericardiocentesis.ts and pressure.ts exist. Mentice Coronary Essentials lists 'Respond to changes in the vital signs' (mentice.com/software/coronary-essentials), and ANGIO Mentor offers 'patient management training with an extensive drug panel and vital signs monitoring' (Surgical Science module list PDF, p. 1).

gaps.area: Mentoring and assessment (transfer to real performance)
gaps.gap: Coaching happens mostly after the case and is rule-based: the dominant mistake maps to generic text. There is no step-level procedure model, no expert benchmarks, no proficiency gates, no expert replay and no spaced scheduling of procedural skills. The PCI debrief is a checklist scored as the percentage of items passed.
gaps.evidence: adaptiveCoach.ts coachCase() counts MistakeCodes and returns MISTAKE_INFO text; CoachPanel.tsx shows the last 7 events and the debrief; angioPci.ts debrief() gives score = 100 * ok / items. Evidence: proficiency-based progression reduced errors by 60%, time by 15% and increased steps by 47% (12 RCTs, 239 participants; Mazzone 2021, doi 10.1097/SLA.0000000000004650). Simulation-based education with deliberate practice had effect size 0.71 against traditional training (McGaghie 2011, doi 10.1097/ACM.0b013e318217e119). Mentored simulation in coronary angiography gave shorter procedure time and lower radiation dose in real cases (Popovic 2019 RCT, doi 10.1016/j.amjcard.2019.01.032). Spaced training improves skill retention (Cecilio-Fernandes 2017, doi 10.1016/j.jsurg.2017.08.002). Mentice advertises 'benchmarking against experts'.
gaps.proposal:
(1) Add a procedure ontology in src/content/procedures/*.ts: for each procedure (diagnostic LCA/RCA, focal PCI, bifurcation, CTO) a task graph of steps, critical and non-critical errors and metrics (time, fluoro time, dose, contrast, runs, coaxiality, stent sizing ratio, edge coverage), validated by the existing content validator.
(2) A live evaluator consumes the store and angioPci event streams and marks steps and errors in real time.
(3) An 'attending in the room' layer asks Socratic questions at decision points, without giving instructions: before inflating, 'Reference diameter? Which view shows both edges?'; after an injection, 'What TIMI flow?'. Answers are checked against simulator ground truth, and prompts can be spoken with speechSynthesis (on device, browser-only).
(4) Expert ghosts: record time-stamped control trajectories from expert runs and overlay and compare them with dynamic time warping. This also strengthens the existing construct-validity test.
(5) Proficiency gates: a module unlocks only after two consecutive attempts at the expert benchmark with zero critical errors.
(6) Extend srs.ts and curriculumEngine.ts so procedural skills come back at spaced intervals.

gaps.gap: Every patient has the same body: habitus 1, heart scale 1, a fixed heart axis, a fixed thorax, and one coronary template with sinusoidal wiggles. Only dominance, a few variants and lesions change.
gaps.evidence: coronaryTree.ts calls makeHeart(1) unconditionally. The thorax.ts habitus option is never passed (grep finds no caller). Base and apex in heart.ts are constants. specsFor() uses fixed surface nodes per vessel. Real population data in the library: AngioCAD (412 patients) has dominance right 326, left 50, unknown 36; indication STEMI 186, stable angina 116, unstable angina 55, NSTEMI 19; mid LAD abnormal in 265/412 and at least 76% stenosed in 174/412; left main normal in 382/412; Gensini median 39.25 (IQR 12-70). Commercial systems import CT/MR for patient-specific rehearsal (Mentice VIST Virtual Patient / Case-It; ANGIO Mentor PROcedure Rehearsal Studio). Open CTA coronary datasets exist: ImageCAS (1,000 CTA with LM/LAD/LCx/RCA labels; I could not confirm its licence on the pages I opened, so verify before use) and ASOCA (licence not verified).

gaps.gap: Coronary motion uses a piecewise contraction envelope that is zero from phase 0.55 to 1.0 and from 0 to 0.08, so there is no diastolic filling motion or atrial kick, and motion is bunched into a short systolic burst. The cardiac silhouette (HEART, HEART_FAT, RVOT, LA and RA shapes) does not beat at all; only breathing moves it. Heart rate is fixed with no variability or ectopy.
gaps.evidence: Real Philips LCA (n = 34, patch tracking at 256 px with ±14 px search): peak-to-peak 29.9 px at 512 (IQR 15.3-48.7, 5.8% of width); P95 frame-to-frame speed 6.2 px/frame (IQR 2.8-11.7); median 2.0 px/frame. Real RCA (n = 6): 38.0 px and 7.2 px/frame. Simulator (vite-node, buildXrayScene + XrayRenderer.project, 230 mm field, 512 px, HR 65, breath held): mid-vessel peak-to-peak 21.9-43.4 px in RAO30/CAU25, 13.1-21.0 px in LAO40/CRA25 and 9.3-32.8 px for the RCA in LAO30; P95 speed 7.6-15.2 px/frame with median 1.0-1.7. Excursion is right, but the timing is too jerky (P95/median about 8-9 in the simulator vs about 3 in real data). Real heart rate from motion autocorrelation: median 65.4 bpm (IQR 60.1-71.5; 35/90 runs with a clear period); sceneBuilder defaults to 72. Code: sceneBuilder.ts contraction(); thorax.ts places anat[ANAT.HEART] from H.base + hs only.
gaps.proposal: Drive the motion from the haemodynamic model: normalise LV volume V(t) from circulation.ts (time-varying elastance activation() already exists) to e(t) = (EDV - V)/(EDV - ESV). This naturally produces ejection, isovolumic relaxation, rapid filling and the atrial kick. Feed e(t) to heart.ts surfacePoint() and also to buildThorax(), so that the HEART, HEART_FAT and RVOT ellipsoid half-axes scale with V(t) and the LA and RA shapes with atrial volume, making the cardiac border pulsate. Add a small pendular translation and rotation of the whole heart, beat-to-beat RR variability, respiratory sinus arrhythmia and ectopics from the rhythm engine. Tune the amplitudes until the motion metrics from the validation harness (excursion and the P95/median speed ratio) match the library per view.

gaps.gap: No dose quantity is computed: no reference air kerma, no dose-area product, no skin-dose map and no operator scatter dose. The scatter-to-primary ratio is a constant 0.75 whatever the field size or patient thickness, and the field size does not affect dose.
gaps.evidence: A grep of src for kerma|mGy|airKerma matches only content and glossary text. angioPci.ts tracks only fluoroS, cineRuns and contrastMl. sceneBuilder.ts fixes counts (cine 1500, fluoro 380) and spr 0.75. The ClarityIQ white paper (pp. 10-13) gives: cardiac fluoro 'typical patient dose rates' of 1.2 (Allura Xper II) and 0.9 / 0.4 / 0.2 mGy/s (AlluraClarity III / II / I) with 0.1/0.1/0.4/0.4 mm Cu and 4/4/4/2 ms pulses; pulse durations kept below 10 ms; typical interventional-cardiology water-equivalent thickness about 25.8 cm (SD 4 cm); air kerma per frame rising steeply with PMMA thickness; air kerma increasing when smaller detector formats are used; and staff dose relative to patient dose of 1.0, 1.2 and 1.36 for no Cu, 0.1 mm and 0.4 mm Cu. Popovic 2019 found lower radiation dose after simulation training, so dose behaviour is a trainable outcome.
gaps.proposal:
Add src/simulation/dose.ts.
- Each frame, take the water-equivalent thickness along the central ray from the anatomy pass. The renderer already computes the line integrals; expose the AEC reference Tref, or compute the path in JS with the same thorax shapes.
- Map thickness and flavour (fluoro I/II/III, cine) to air kerma per pulse using curves digitised from the white paper's figures, with the source cited in code. Scale by pulse rate, by field size (detector format factor) and by SID through the inverse square law to the interventional reference point.
- Accumulate Ka,r, and compute KAP = Ka,r x field area.
- Keep a skin-dose map on a cylindrical back-of-patient grid indexed by beam entrance point per C-arm angle, which teaches angle rotation.
- Estimate operator dose as KAP times a projection- and position-dependent scatter factor, times shielding (ceiling shield and table skirt toggles).
- Close the loop: the photon count in DISPLAY_FS comes from the dose per pulse, so a lower dose gives a noisier image, and SPR is computed from field area and thickness, so collimation visibly cuts scatter and dose.
- Show Ka,r and KAP live in the HUD and the debrief.

gaps.area: Physiology and intravascular imaging inside the cath lab
gaps.gap: Pressure-wire physiology (physiology.ts) and IVUS/OCT (pciBench.ts) are separate benches. Neither is driven by the angiographic lesion and wire position in the cath-lab PCI, and there is no co-registration with the angiogram.
gaps.evidence: angioPci.ts imports only BALLOON_SPEC and the balloon/stent diameter functions from pciBench.ts, and has no physiology import. The roadmap's 'still to do' includes 'intracoronary imaging linked to the angiographic lesion'. The Philips iFR co-registration workflow (philips.com quick guide PDF) is a pullback under continuous fluoro (optimal 15 pulses/s, minimum 7.5), then an angiogram with the same table and C-arm geometry for roadmap selection, with values mapped onto the angiogram. The Philips coronary suite page lists IntraSight ('imaging, physiology and co-registration tools'), iFR and IVUS.
gaps.proposal: In angioPci.ts add a pressure wire, which is a variant of the 0.014 rod with a sensor 3 cm from the tip. Build the physiology.ts CoronaryCase from the same TreeVessel radii and lesions along the route, and compute Pd/Pa, wave-free ratio and FFR (with adenosine through the patient engine) at the sensor's path position. A pullback under fluoro records (path mm, ratio), tracks the sensor marker on the image, and draws co-registered dots on a stored cine frame. For IVUS, generate cross-sections with pciBench.preImaging()-style models from the local lumen radius, an EEM derived from the reference vessel and the lesion's calcium arc, track the transducer marker on fluoro during a motorised pullback, and co-register. Use both to teach a physiology-guided decision (treat or defer), landing zones, stent length and post-PCI optimisation, all on the same anatomy the fellow just wired.

gaps.gap: The drills are run-level multiple choice (grade, artery, view, dominance, occlusion, collaterals). There is no lesion localisation on the image, no segment naming, no teaching of inter-observer and QCA disagreement, no 'what view next' planning drill, and no sim-to-real view matching.
gaps.evidence: RealAngiograms.tsx DrillKind is 'grade' | 'artery' | 'view' | 'dominance' | 'occlusion' | 'collaterals'. Available labels: CADICA runs carry keyframes, worst and boxes (lesion boxes); AngioCAD has 15-segment grades for 412 patients; CoronaryDominance has angles on 1,625 runs. Real view usage (CoronaryDominance, ±15° families): LCA (n = 1,239) AP 22.9%, RAO-CRA 13.7%, AP-CAU 13.3%, LAO-CAU 12.1%, AP-CRA 11.9%, RAO 9.8%, LAO-CRA 8.9%; RCA (n = 386) LAO 70.5%, AP-CRA 12.4%, LAO-CRA 9.1%; median 5 LCA and 1 RCA runs per study (277 studies). ARCADE (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.10390295) is CC0 with 26-region SYNTAX-style vessel masks and stenosis annotations in COCO format, opened at openaire. Visual estimation disagrees: inter-operator kappa 0.26-0.58 by category and no concordance with QCA percentage diameter stenosis (Sen 2018, doi 10.5830/CVJA-2018-024); visual and QCA agreement kappa 0.22-0.44 (Dou 2016, doi 10.4244/EIJV11I14A311).
gaps.proposal:
(1) Click-to-localise drill: CADICA boxes, scored by intersection-over-union, on the keyframe of the run.
(2) Name-the-segment drill: with the user's download approval, add ARCADE (CC0) to the library through a build_arcade.py following the existing build scripts. Click a vessel and name its SYNTAX segment; masks score the answer.
(3) A calibration drill that shows your estimate, the dataset label and the published spread of inter-observer agreement, so fellows learn the uncertainty of eyeballing.
(4) Plan-the-next-view drill: show a patient's first runs, ask which projection to take next, and compare with the real sequence and angles.
(5) Sim-twin: for a real run, set the simulator to the real primary and secondary angles, render the synthetic patient, and toggle between the two. This builds the 3D mental model and doubles as the realism test in the validation-harness gap.

gaps.gap: No feature turns two or more runs into 3D understanding: no reconstruction from two projections, no foreshortening or overlap map across C-arm space, and no feedback that a lesion was judged in a foreshortened or overlapped view.
gaps.evidence: projection.ts already exports elongation(points3d, basis) and cone-beam projection. The roadmap item A10 asks for at least two orthogonal views before a severity call and for the effect of foreshortening that hides a stenosis. The cine store (useCineStore.ts) keeps runs, but nothing analyses them across views.
gaps.proposal: After any two cine runs of the same artery, triangulate the target vessel centreline from the two simulated projections by epipolar matching of the projected samples. Use the true samples, but add the error a real reconstruction would have from the angle separation and the overlap, so that small separations visibly give poor depth. Display a rotatable 3D tree, a per-view foreshortening and overlap heat map over LAO/RAO x CRA/CAU (computing elongation() plus a branch-overlap test for each grid cell, for example at 5° steps), and the 'optimal view' for the target segment. Score whether the fellow's views met it. Link to the stenosis-grading feedback: 'you called 50% in a view with 40% foreshortening'.

gaps.area: Detector noise texture and processing profiles
gaps.gap: Quantum noise is drawn from bilinearly interpolated Gaussian hashes on a 0.75x grid, with fixed counts, so its strength and spatial correlation do not match any real system. Real systems differ a great deal by vendor and processing.
gaps.evidence: Residual noise (frame 2, central 60%, sigma-clipped residual against Gaussian blur sigma 1.2, as stored after JPEG q72), median (IQR): CoronaryDominance sigma 4.64 (3.85-5.41), lag-1 0.157, lag-2 -0.121; dominance-main 7.46 (7.27-7.68), lag-1 -0.149; CADICA (Siemens) 0.81 (0.37-1.09), lag-1 0.192; AngioCAD 2.16 (1.35-2.70), lag-1 0.226. Simulator, same method after browser JPEG 0.72: sigma 1.69-2.69 with lag-1 0.365-0.404 at 25 cm across five views (raw, 20 cm: sigma 2.94-3.63, lag-1 0.08-0.21). XrayRenderer.ts vnoise() interpolates gauss() on uv*uRes*0.75.
gaps.proposal: Generate noise at detector-pixel resolution with an independent Gaussian per pixel. Shape it with a small separable kernel whose taps are solved so that lag-1 and lag-2 match each processing profile, standing in for the detector MTF and NPS. Set its variance from the photon count per pixel supplied by the dose model (dose-physics gap), and add an electronic-noise floor. Apply the noise before the spatial noise reduction and harmonisation of the processing-chain gap, so that the processed image ends up with the measured sigma and correlation. Fit per profile against realism_targets.json, and expose fluoro flavours I/II/III as real noise and dose trade-offs.

gaps.area: X-ray physics fidelity (spectrum, scatter, geometric blur)
gaps.gap: Attenuation uses a single effective energy, and iodine and metal 'gain' come from a heuristic kV formula. There is no polychromatic beam, beam hardening or copper filtration. Scatter is one blurred copy of the primary at a fixed SPR. There is no focal-spot penumbra, so vessels near the tube are as sharp as those near the detector.
gaps.evidence: sceneBuilder.ts: kv = 62 + (path - 220) * 0.12 and gain = (75/kv)^2.2, with spr 0.75 constant. TRANS_FS computes exp(-(a.r + uIodine*a.g + uMetal*a.b)). DISPLAY_FS takes scatter as textureLod(uTrans, uv, 5.5). The ClarityIQ white paper discusses copper filtration removing 'soft radiation', small versus large focal spots (0.4 vs 0.7 for FD20, 0.5 vs 0.8 for FD10) and their penumbra (Fig. 20), and pulse length against motion blur. DeepDRR (arXiv 1803.08606) obtains realistic radiographs from material decomposition, analytic forward projection, learned scatter and noise injection.
gaps.proposal: Keep the three material channels already accumulated (R soft and bone, G iodine, B metal) and add a fourth for bone-only path length, using an RGBA32F target. In TRANS_FS evaluate a 3-4 bin spectrum: T = Σ_b w_b(kV, Cu) exp(-Σ_m μ_m(E_b) L_m), with μ/ρ tables obtained from NIST XCOM and cited in code, not typed from memory. Iodine contrast then falls with kV and patient thickness on its own, and copper changes contrast and dose. Model scatter as a two-Gaussian kernel (short and long range) on the mip chain, with SPR from field area and water-equivalent thickness and a grid transmission factor. Add geometric blur in the tube pass: per-vertex blur radius = focal spot x (SID - SOD_object)/SOD_object, implemented by widening the ribbon and softening the profile, and add motion blur from pulse width x projected speed.

gaps.area: Non-anatomical image content (what makes real cines look real)
gaps.gap: The simulated patient carries no external or implanted hardware. Real cath-lab images routinely contain ECG electrodes and lead wires, sternal wires and clips after CABG, pacemaker or ICD leads, prosthetic valves and table edges, and their absence is a strong 'synthetic' cue.
gaps.evidence: datasets/ATTRIBUTION.md, from the screening of library frames, states 'Frames show anatomy and devices only (catheters, wires, sternal wires, pacing leads, prosthetic valves)'. thorax.ts builds only anatomy plus pulmonary vessel trees, and sceneBuilder adds only catheters, the wire and PCI devices.

gaps.area: Complications and bifurcation consequences as image physics
gaps.gap: Complications are latched flags with log messages and simple rendered blobs (a false channel, growing extravasation). There is no side-branch jailing or occlusion, no plaque shift, no propagating dissection, no air embolus in the image, and no thrombus that embolises distally.
gaps.evidence: angioPci.ts uses dissection, perforation, slowFlow and geographicMiss flags, with geometric thresholds such as dBal/localRef > 1.2. pciDevices() in AngioPci.tsx draws 'a contrast-filled false channel beside the lumen' and 'extravasated contrast that grows with each injection'. The roadmap says side-branch jailing and bifurcation techniques are still to do. Risk of side-branch occlusion can be scored from angiographic features (V-RESOLVE: occlusion in 16.7% of high-risk vs 4.3% of non-high-risk lesions, doi 10.4244/EIJV11I14A311). ANGIO Mentor offers 'pre-programmed as well as dynamic complications' and a bifurcation module (Surgical Science PDF).

gaps.gap: Control is mouse, keyboard and on-screen buttons. The haptics layer has pseudo-haptics and gamepad rumble, but WebHID is a stub that reports itself unavailable. There is no two-handed control (one hand fixing the wire while the other advances a device), no foot pedal and no torquer.
gaps.evidence: haptics.ts: WebHIDHapticsAdapter has 'readonly available = false', with the comment 'Wiring point for a real haptic torquer'. CatheterHub.tsx maps vertical and horizontal drag to insertion and torque. AngioPci.tsx uses buttons and key steps. SimCath's main hardware investment is 'a redesigned haptic interface supporting multiple-port interventions' and 'a motorized mock C-arm' (Imperial page). Imperial's earlier work found that senior clinicians felt existing simulators did not resemble real forces (imperial.ac.uk/simms procedure modelling page).
gaps.proposal:
Browser-only, low-cost hardware path:
(1) Gamepad API with two sticks and triggers: left stick for wire push and torque, right trigger for device push, left trigger for syringe flow, and the bumpers as pedals for fluoro and cine. Rumble is already supported, so deliver contact-force pulses from the rod constraint impulses.
(2) WebHID or WebSerial for a DIY torquer: a rotary encoder for torque plus a linear potentiometer or optical sensor for push, read from a microcontroller. Replace the stub with a documented report format.
(3) A USB foot pedal recognised as HID keys for F and Space.
(4) Map forces from the rod model to pseudo-haptic gain (haptics.gain()) and to rumble amplitude, so feel and image come from one physical source.

gaps.area: Roadmap and stent-enhancement tools taught as part of the workflow
gaps.gap: There is no motion-compensated roadmap and no marker-based stent enhancement, so the fellow cannot practise contrast-saving navigation or confirm stent expansion the way it is done on modern systems.
gaps.evidence: The Philips coronary suite page says Dynamic Coronary Roadmap gives 'motion-compensated, real-time navigational guidance' and 'reduces contrast agent use by 28.8%'. DCR4Contrast (EuroIntervention, 356 randomised) reported contrast 64.6±44.4 vs 90.8±55.4 mL and cine runs 8.7±4.7 vs 11.7±7.6, with no significant difference in fluoroscopy time or air kerma. StentBoost works by detecting the two balloon markers per frame and warping and averaging frames to show the stent (described in Philips StentBoost search material and literature). No such feature exists in src/ui/sections/AngioPci.tsx.
gaps.proposal: Implement both as generic, ECG-gated teaching tools, not a copy of any vendor's design. Roadmap: after a cine, store one mask per cardiac phase bin (16 bins) from the rendered iodine channel, and during fluoro overlay the mask for the current ECG phase. Breathing mismatch shows when the patient is not holding their breath, which teaches its limits. Count contrast saved. Stent enhancement: acquire about 2 s of cine with the balloon in place, detect the two marker bands (positions known to the simulator, with simulated detection noise), register by similarity transform and average, which reveals under-expansion and stent edges. Both feed the dose and contrast scoring.

gaps.gap: The lab is silent and solitary. There is no radiographer or nurse to instruct, no closed-loop communication, no C-arm movement limits or travel time, and no environment cues. SimCath and ANGIO Mentor Suite both emphasise team training.
gaps.evidence: The SimCath page targets interventional and non-interventional (anaesthetics) clinicians, with a 'motorized mock C-arm'. ANGIO Mentor lists team training and simulation of C-arm and table operation. In CathMaster, view presets jump instantly (setCArm(v.cArm) in AngioPci.tsx).
gaps.proposal:
(1) Command interface: typed or spoken orders ('pan up', 'LAO 30 cranial 30', 'nitrate 200 micrograms intracoronary', 'ACT please') parsed into actions, with replies from a virtual radiographer or nurse through speechSynthesis. Speech recognition is optional; in Chrome it may send audio to a remote service, so it must be opt-in and disclosed.
(2) C-arm kinematics with angular speed limits and isocentre, so view changes take time and cost fluoro.
(3) Ambient audio (pulse-oximeter tone pitched to SpO2, alarms) driven by the patient engine.
(4) Crisis drills (VF, tamponade, no-reflow) with team actions timed in the debrief.

gaps.gap: Even with physically fitted statistics, residual texture differences (parenchymal and lung texture, processing artefacts) may still betray simulated frames. Nothing learned from real data is applied to the images.
gaps.evidence: The anatomy pass uses procedural fbm noise sampled at the ray midpoint (ANAT_FS, 'tex = fbm(mid * 0.035) ...'), not texture integrated along the ray. DeepDRR (arXiv 1803.08606) reports that models trained on its physics-based synthetic radiographs generalised to real data without domain adaptation, which suggests that physics plus learned components can approach real appearance. This environment has no numpy or training stack.
gaps.proposal: Treat this as phase 2, after the validation-harness gap exists to measure it. Train offline (outside the browser) a small residual network in the log-intensity domain on unpaired sim and real frames, with a geometry-preserving loss (vessel and device masks from the renderer must not move). Export it to ONNX and run it with ONNX Runtime Web on WebGL or WebGPU at 512 px, only on the background, low-frequency bands of the pyramid from the processing-chain gap, so it cannot invent or erase vessels. Ship it only if blinded discrimination accuracy falls and the geometric metrics are unchanged; otherwise keep the purely physical chain.
