tasks.acceptance: No XP, level title or streak text remains anywhere in the UI (grep). Old profiles load without loss of attempt history.
tasks.verify: progress.test.ts migration test; grep for 'XP', 'streak' and 'CathMaster' level strings.

tasks.title: Simulator logbook
tasks.detail: Each case records the indication, access route, catheters and devices, runs, fluoro time, Ka,r and KAP, contrast, complications, mode and role. The logbook is exportable as JSON or CSV, mirroring the content's logbook lesson.
tasks.acceptance: Every finished session in either lab writes one logbook row. recordSim best-score-only calls are replaced.

tasks.title: EPA entrustment
tasks.detail:
competency.ts defines 12 EPAs, each described with ten Cate's 8 sections:
- access-radial and access-femoral
- lca-engage and rca-engage
- diag-study and diag-report
- lesion-assess
- pci-simple, pci-calcium, pci-stemi and pci-cto
- complication-bailout

Levels map to EAPCI I-V. Rules:
- A level is awarded only after N exam-mode passes on distinct unseen cases, spread over at least 2 days, with zero critical errors.
- Levels expire if a skill is not practised, which schedules a refresher.
- The level drives the VisibilityPolicy and mentor fading.
- recordExam is finally called.
- Level 10 'pass Master Assessment' is enforced.
tasks.acceptance: Unit tests cover awarding, refusal on a critical error, refusal for passes on the same day, and expiry.

tasks.title: Competency case ladders and held-out exam pool
tasks.detail:
catalogue.ts builds, for each EPA, rungs 1-6 from generateBatch(preset, seed, n) sorted by caseDifficultyAxes (progressive difficulty; Grover 2017).

- Passing a rung's standard twice unlocks the next rung.
- Mastered rungs are interleaved for retention.
- Exam seeds are held out and never appear in practice.
- The daily challenge is the next rung of the weakest due EPA.
- Blocked practice per EPA per day is capped, so practice is spread out (Moulton 2006).
tasks.acceptance: Ladders are monotone in difficulty, and exam seeds never appear in practice sets.

tasks.title: Three-part module mastery
tasks.detail:
Module mastery has three parts, shown separately in Pathway:
- knowledge: quiz memory with at least 2 reps
- skill: passes on the linked EPA rungs
- image reading: balanced accuracy on the linked real drills

Module.evidence links each module to EPAs and standards.
tasks.acceptance: A PCI module cannot reach 100% without passing its skill evidence.

streams.title: Real-angiogram reading drills and content integrity
streams.goal: Make the real-image drills impossible to beat by guessing, fix the scoring bug, add localisation and calibration, and remove the answer-length giveaway and non-branching cases from the Academy.
touchesSharedFiles: src/simulation/srs.ts (owner S12): QuizMemory items keyed by run id

tasks.title: Fix CADICA stenosis-degree scoring
tasks.detail: normalise() and DEGREE_OPTIONS in RealAngiograms.tsx (~219) do not match the dataset labels '> 70%', '>70%' and '20-50%'. Fix the mismatch and use the dataset's native classes: <20%, 20-50% and >70%.
tasks.acceptance: All 42 of 42 CADICA patients can be scored correct (now 6 of 42).
tasks.verify: Unit test iterating datasets/library/cadica/index.json maxDegree values.

tasks.title: Stratified drills, balanced accuracy, kappa and projection ambiguity
tasks.detail:
Sample items stratified by class, with equal positives and negatives per set. Report balanced accuracy and Cohen's kappa against the expert label.

In the projection drill, drop runs within 5 degrees of a standardView boundary (34.7% of runs) or accept either neighbouring view, and show the recorded angles as feedback.

These changes neutralise the guessing base rates: always 'right dominant' 77.9%, always 'LCA' 71.8%, always 'normal' 74.3%.
tasks.acceptance: A constant-answer strategy scores 50% balanced accuracy and kappa of 0 in every drill.

tasks.title: Locate-the-lesion drill with confidence calibration
tasks.detail:
On a CADICA keyframe the learner clicks the lesion. It is a hit if the click is inside the expert box with a 10% margin. Detection and grading are scored separately.

- A confidence slider per answer.
- A Brier score and signed over- or under-calling bias for stenosis grade.
- Each run id becomes an SRS item.
- Per-item results are saved for learning curves.
- SimIds 'angio-real' and 'angio-pci' are added with parameters, so modules can link to specific drills.
tasks.acceptance: The drill works on all CADICA runs with boxes. Brier score and bias are shown, and wrong reads return through SRS.
tasks.verify: Manual run plus unit test of the hit test.

tasks.title: Next-view planning and inter-observer calibration drills
tasks.detail:
Next-view planning: show the first runs of a real study, ask for the next projection, and compare with the real sequence and angles.

Calibration: show the learner's estimate next to the label and the published inter-observer spread (Sen 2018, doi 10.5830/CVJA-2018-024).
tasks.acceptance: Both drills run on CoronaryDominance studies with at least 3 runs.

tasks.title: Remove the answer-length cue and add consequence branches
tasks.detail:
Add a validate.ts rule: fail a module where the correct option is longer than 1.3 times the mean distractor, or is uniquely the longest, in more than 35% of items (a project rule).

- Rewrite the flagged distractors: 352 of 542 quiz items are currently uniquely longest.
- Give cases consequence steps (CaseOption.next pointing to a complication or recovery step) and a stateDelta, so non-best choices compound. Currently 0 of 257 steps branch.
- Add 'cine' blocks using the real library.
- Store item analytics locally (p-value and point-biserial correlation).
tasks.acceptance: content.test.ts passes the new rule. An always-pick-longest strategy scores close to chance. At least 30% of case steps branch.

tasks.title: Segment-naming drill on ARCADE (gated)
tasks.detail:
Gated: only after the user approves the download and the CC0 licence is confirmed at the Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.10390295.

Then:
- write scripts/angio_library/build_arcade.py, following the existing build scripts
- add a click-a-vessel, name-its-SYNTAX-segment drill scored by the masks
- update ATTRIBUTION.md
tasks.acceptance: The drill scores against masks, and attribution is recorded.
tasks.verify: Manual run after an approved download.

streams.title: PCI procedure realism: equipment, coronary wire, physiology, imaging and complications
streams.goal: Make PCI an equipment workflow on physical rods. Wire steering, device delivery, inflation, physiology and IVUS run on the same anatomy, and complications evolve physically with prodromes and bailouts.
ownsFiles: src/simulation/pci/renderDevices.ts (new; moves pciDevices out of AngioPci.tsx)
src/simulation/complications/ (new: engine.ts, dissection.ts, perforation.ts, sideBranch.ts, airEmbolism.ts, noReflow.ts, thrombus.ts)
src/ui/pci/ (new: EquipmentTray.tsx, BoxLabel.tsx, Indeflator.tsx, PhysiologyConsole.tsx, IvusView.tsx, LesionCalipers.tsx)
touchesSharedFiles: src/ui/sections/AngioPci.tsx (owner S10): mount EquipmentTray, Indeflator, PhysiologyConsole, IvusView and LesionCalipers in LabLayout slots; call renderDevices() instead of local pciDevices (lines 572-650)
src/render/xray/coronaryTree.ts (owner S3b): runtime radius and lumen modifiers for a dissection false lumen and side-branch ostial narrowing through the existing lesion-modifier path
src/simulation/physiology.ts (owner S9): build CoronaryCase from TreeVessel radii and lesions

tasks.title: Coronary wire on the rod solver
tasks.detail:
The 0.014 wire is a rod in the moving coronary lumens (S7 core):
- a tip-shaping step (primary and secondary bend angle and length)
- torque transmitted through the guide and proximal bends, with lag and whip
- tip load and stiffness per wire kind from wires.ts
- the lesion cap as a resistance field: penetration happens when tip axial force exceeds cap strength, and subintimal probability rises with tip load and off-axis force
- visible prolapse and knuckling
- distal migration when devices advance

This replaces the cos > 0.6 branch rule, instant torque and the binary canCross.
tasks.acceptance: Branch entry depends on 3D tip orientation relative to the take-off. A septal-branch entry is possible with a shaped tip. A distal-excursion metric is recorded.

tasks.title: Equipment workflow and guide support
tasks.detail:
The guide starts unengaged. The workflow:
1. Request a device through the nurse (S15) or the tray.
2. Check the box label.
3. Prepare the balloon (negative pressure).
4. Backload it on the pinned wire.
5. Open the haemostatic valve, which drops out the tip pressure.
6. Advance with friction. The guide reaction force backs the guide out unless backup (guide family, depth, opposite-wall contact) is sufficient.

RX vs OTW, guide extension and a buddy wire are available.
tasks.acceptance: Advancing a stiff device through a calcified bend with a poorly seated JR backs the guide out, while an EBU-type guide holds. An unpinned wire migrates.

tasks.title: Indeflator, inflation and positioning
tasks.detail:
The screw rate sets the pressure rise along the pciBench compliance (balloonDiameter).

- Inflation time accrues territory ischaemia (S9).
- Rapid inflation in a rubbery lesion causes melon-seeding.
- Deflation to full negative takes time.
- Marker bands work as a ruler.
- Contrast puffs through the guide position the stent.
- NC post-dilation inside the stent.
tasks.acceptance: The rated-burst-pressure, rupture and dissection hazards come from exposures. Ischaemia and ST elevation appear during inflation.

tasks.title: Procedural stent geometry
tasks.detail:
Rings of zig-zag struts with crowns, plus connectors, are built in vessel-local coordinates (s, theta) and mapped onto the deployed centreline at each ring's balloon- or vessel-limited radius. They are rendered through ThinPrims (S2b).

- Markers are Pt-Ir thick-wall cylinders.
- Under-expansion, malapposition, overlap, foreshortening and longitudinal compression are all visible.
- Ring counts and strut thickness are device parameters taken from IFUs, with sources cited.
tasks.acceptance: A stent under-expanded by 20% shows a visibly narrower ring envelope in marker-enhanced images (S10).
tasks.verify: Unit test of ring radii; visual capture.

tasks.title: Pressure wire and IVUS on the same anatomy
tasks.detail:
Pressure wire:
- The sensor sits 3 cm from the tip.
- physiology.reading() and indices() are evaluated on a CoronaryCase built from TreeVessel radii and lesions.
- The workflow is equalise, check drift, adenosine (with AV block via S9), then pullback recorded as a series and co-registered on a stored frame.

IVUS: a motorised pullback generates cross-sections from the local lumen, a reference-derived EEM and the calcium arc, with the transducer marker tracked on fluoro and co-registered to the angiogram.

Post-stent re-measurement updates the lesion coefficients.
tasks.acceptance: FFR and the angiographic transit are consistent, both coming from the same flow(). Pullback dots map to the correct segments within 2 mm.

tasks.title: Physical complication engine
tasks.detail:
Each complication has:
- exposures from physics: wall-contact force integral, injection pressure, oversize ratio, pressure vs RBP, tip load in small branches, conus contrast, air volume
- a hazard function with a seeded draw for replay
- prodromes: pressure, symptom or image cue
- progression
- bailout actions with effects

The complications:
- Dissection is a second lumen that retains contrast (staining) and extends with forceful injection.
- Perforation is an Ellis-type jet whose leak rate fills the pericardium, leading to tamponade and pericardiocentesis.ts.
- Side-branch occlusion comes from carina shift driven by plaque, bifurcation angle and stent-to-vessel ratio.
- Air bubbles are advected and cause ST elevation and bradycardia.
- Thrombus embolises to distal twigs, causing slow flow.

Bailouts include prolonged inflation, covered stent, protamine, pacing and defibrillation. These follow the Brilakis principles in docs/reference.
tasks.acceptance: Each complication shows a prodrome, progresses if untreated and responds to the correct bailout. Draws are reproducible in replay.
tasks.verify: Complication unit tests with fixed seeds.

tasks.title: Lesion assessment, sizing rationale and ACT
tasks.detail:
On a frozen end-diastolic frame the learner places calipers for the proximal and distal reference, the MLD and the length. Errors are scored against ground truth, and QCA is revealed only afterwards.

The learner chooses a sizing basis (distal reference, mean reference or imaging). ACT is checked before device advance in supervised mode. PciMetrics feed S11, replacing the percentage-of-checklist debrief.
tasks.acceptance: The debrief reports the lesion estimate error in mm and the sizing ratio. The old checklist score is gone.

streams.title: Team, conscious patient, voice and audio
streams.goal: Add the lab's people and sounds: closed-loop communication with nurse, radiographer, physiologist, anaesthetist and a talking patient, plus monitor, exposure and device sounds driven by physics.
touchesSharedFiles: src/ui/lab/LabLayout.tsx (owner S10): mount CommandPalette (Ctrl/Cmd-K) and Captions in the reserved slots
src/content/tracks/complications.ts (owner S13): add links from crisis lessons to the matching drills

tasks.title: Team and patient agents
tasks.detail:
Each Agent has a role, a perception scope (the physiologist sees the monitor, the scrub nurse sees the table and inventory, the radiographer sees the C-arm and dose, the patient has sensations), a speech queue with latency, and memory.

- Read-backs are logged with timestamps, for example 'heparin 5,000 units given at 10:32'.
- Fetched equipment arrives after a delay.
- Rare wrong-item events require a label check.
- The patient speaks: pain at puncture, burning with the cocktail, chest pain on inflation, nausea in a vagal reaction, distress with adenosine.
tasks.acceptance: Every order produces a read-back. Communication quality (closed loops, patient warned before adenosine or inflation) is scored in the S11 debrief.

tasks.title: Command input
tasks.detail:
The typed command palette is the primary input. Push-to-talk Web Speech recognition is opt-in, with an on-screen disclosure that the browser may process audio on a remote service.

The intent grammar covers:
- drug, dose and route
- device requests
- breath commands
- C-arm and table
- 'I have the wire'

All features are feature-detected.
tasks.acceptance: Twenty scripted utterances parse to the correct intents. The typed fallback covers every intent.

tasks.title: Audio engine
tasks.detail:
Web Audio provides:
- a monitor QRS beep locked to the CardiacClock, pitched to SpO2
- alarm tones at thresholds
- an exposure tone while any pedal is emitting
- syringe and plunger sounds scaled by flow and pressure
- indeflator ratchet clicks, valve and flush sounds
- team and patient voices

All sounds start only after a user gesture.
tasks.acceptance: The beep aligns with the ECG R wave within 20 ms, and the exposure tone stops when the pedal is released.
tasks.verify: Timestamp check in dev; manual listening.

streams.title: Continuous case session: preparation, access and closure
streams.goal: One case from arrival to handover on one clock: chart review, time-out, physical access under ultrasound and fluoroscopy, flushing and exchanges, continuous engagement and ad hoc PCI, then closure and delayed complications.
touchesSharedFiles: src/state/useSimulatorStore.ts (owner S10): replace toEngage -> loadCase(caseData) handover (useProcedureStore 158-163) with session continuation; PCI initial state continues from the session instead of 'guide engaged at t=0'
src/render/xray/thorax.ts (owner S4): forearm, brachial and subclavian anatomy within the field for table pans along the radial route

tasks.title: CaseSession checklist
tasks.detail:
The trainee drives the session in any order. It replaces PHASE_ORDER and covers:
- chart review (allergies, eGFR, anticoagulants, weight)
- the team time-out
- orders: sedation, heparin, radial cocktail
- exchanges as physical sequences on the rods: J-wire, track catheter, pull wire with back-bleed, aspirate to waste, flush, connect to the manifold, zero and level, check the aortic trace

Each step takes real time. Each omission has a physical consequence: air embolism, wrong pressures, catheter thrombus, radial occlusion.
tasks.acceptance: Skipping a flush leaves air in the line, which raises the air-embolism hazard. Not zeroing gives offset pressures. Diagnostic angiography continues straight into ad hoc PCI with the same access, heparin, contrast and dose totals.

tasks.title: Ultrasound-guided puncture
tasks.detail:
ultrasound.ts renders a synthetic B-mode of the artery and venae comitantes in cross-section and long axis: the artery pulsates and the veins compress. It includes needle position, angle and offset, needle reflection and tissue tenting.

- Flashback in the hub is pulsatile only when the needle tip is in the lumen.
- Back-wall puncture and a subintimal wire are possible.
- The radial site is 2-3 cm above the wrist crease (StatPearls).

The depth slider, FeedStage progress bars, schematic route and TipDial are deleted.
tasks.acceptance: A front-wall puncture with pulsatile flashback lets the wire advance. A back-wall puncture gives resistance and the patient reports pain.

tasks.title: Wire navigation on fluoroscopy
tasks.detail:
The trainee navigates with table pans over the forearm, shoulder and arch on the real renderer, using S7 lumens.

- Radial diameter is a state that shrinks with contact force and anxiety (spasm) and recovers after the cocktail.
- Subclavian tortuosity straightens with a deep breath.
- A wire in the descending aorta is corrected in LAO.
tasks.acceptance: The radial-to-root route can be completed on fluoroscopy alone, and spasm appears with forceful manipulation.

tasks.title: Closure and handover
tasks.detail:
Remove devices and the sheath. Apply a radial band (inflation volume, patent haemostasis check with oximetry) or femoral manual compression or a closure device.

Heparin, ACT and sheath size drive a haematoma hazard that can present minutes later at handover. The trainee writes a handover note, which is compared with ground truth.
tasks.acceptance: Closure is required to finish the case, and delayed bleeding can present.

removeOrChange: Remove the always-visible coach line and status chips in Simulator.tsx (lines ~150-157, 238-243) and the raw eng.kind codes in CoachPanel.tsx (~65). Engagement state is inferred from image, pressure and feel; explanations appear only in the Teach-mode attending drawer.

risks: The cranial/caudal sign fix (S1) invalidates every view-dependent calibration already done, including the earlier DRC 0.7 / level -0.12 fit and the LAO cranial grey offset. S2 auto-window and all scorecard captures must be taken after S1 lands, or the work has to be repeated.

There is no git, so parallel streams risk clobbering each other. Each stream writes only the files it owns. The integrator takes a dated copy of the project before each wave and applies the listed shared-file edits serially, running tsc, vitest and the realism scorecard after each one.

The audits' absolute noise and contrast numbers differ by measurement method. Examples: Azurion SD 3.28 lossless temporal versus 5.55 on the 512/JPEG flattest-block pipeline versus 4.64 as a residual against blur; contrast arrival 0.40 s at the 10% threshold versus 0.73 s at 30%. Targets must always be checked with the same script and pipeline that defined them (realism_targets.json is tagged by pipeline), or tuning will chase the wrong value.

Calibration may overfit to few patients or one vendor. Motion and vessel-profile targets come from 1-2 patients per vessel. Pixel scale assumes a 6F catheter (a 17% difference if 5F), and the Azurion frames were cropped and resized by the dataset authors. Prefer ratios and distribution bands, and widen samples before fitting tightly.

Frame budget. The rod worker, 3D clutter ray-march, segment integrator, pyramid, spectral stage and motion blur together could exceed 15 fps on integrated GPUs. Each pass is timed with renderer.perf.ts, with an automatic 768 fallback and adaptive rod node counts. Spectral and motion blur are the first to be disabled.

WebGL2 extension availability (EXT_color_buffer_float, EXT_float_blend, EXT_disjoint_timer_query) varies. The fallbacks are RGBA16F with offsets and CPU timing, and they must be tested on a non-Apple GPU.

Rod physics is the hardest and longest task (effort 5). Until it is calibrated, engagement may feel worse than the current scripted model. Keep engagement.ts's old computeTip behind a flag until the manoeuvre tests pass, and require clinician review of each manoeuvre signature.
Deterministic replay requires bit-stable physics across worker scheduling. Use fixed timesteps, seeded random numbers and an input log with tick stamps, and test replay equality in CI.
Removing scaffolding (meters, coach line, QCA) may frustrate novices. Teach mode keeps explanations in the attending drawer, and the visibility policy fades with entrustment rather than all at once.

Many physiological magnitudes still need primary sources: response time constants, drug effects, dose program curves, catheter stiffness, device IFU dimensions and heart phase timing. Nothing ships with typed-from-memory numbers. Each is recorded in docs/SIM_FACTS.md with a source, or explicitly labelled as a fitted model parameter.

There is a citation conflict in the audits. The benchmark audit attributes both visual-QCA kappa 0.22-0.44 ('Dou 2016') and V-RESOLVE side-branch occlusion to the same DOI, 10.4244/EIJV11I14A311. Verify before citing either, and use Sen 2018 for inter-observer spread until resolved.

Dataset licences. ARCADE (stated CC0) and any CT-derived trees (ImageCAS, ASOCA licences unverified) need licence confirmation and the user's explicit download approval before use. No patient pixels may ever be embedded as textures; only statistics are kept.
Web Speech recognition in Chrome may send audio to a remote service. It must be opt-in with a disclosure, and the typed command palette must cover every intent.

Vendor similarity. Processing profiles, roadmap and marker enhancement must stay generic, published-principle implementations with neutral names and UI, and must never reproduce proprietary layouts or algorithms.

Scope. 19 streams is a lot. If capacity is limited, prioritise S1, S2, S2b, S3a, S3b, S4 and S0 (image realism), then S10 and S11 (removing game feel and adding the mentor), then S7 (rods), before S14-S16.

critique:
Below are corrections to the build plan. I checked them against the code in `/Users/qc25212/Downloads/Misc/Games and apps/Cath Simulator` and the library `index.json` files. I modified no project files. The one scratch script is `/private/tmp/claude-502/cathmaster-research/critique/count.ts`, run with vite-node.

## A. Sequencing and dependencies

1. **Add a wave 0 before any parallel work.** It should contain:
   - a dated copy of the project and a baseline scorecard captured from that copy;
   - the S1 sign fix and its tests;
   - S0 `xrayCapture.ts`;
   - the S2 slot refactor, bit-identical, with stub files for `clutter.ts` and `segments/`.

   Without it, S2 writes stubs into files owned by S4 and S2b, and S2 tunes the auto-window before the sign fix, which the plan's own first risk forbids.
2. **Capture-based acceptance in wave 1 cannot be met inside wave 1.** `buildXrayScene` (owned by S5, wave 2) is the only route from S2b, S3a, S3b and S4 into a frame. Each wave-1 stream should be accepted on unit and headless tests only. Add an owned "integration and calibration" stream after each wave that runs the scorecard and owns fixing metrics that need several streams. Examples:
   - S3b's opacified area of 16-34% also needs S5 transport and S2 processing.
   - S2b's w80/w20 profile needs S2's MTF and S5's streaming parameters.
3. **Declare the missing dependencies.**
   - S3b depends on S3a: S3b consumes groove curves from S3a and the `Motion` type from `heart.ts`, which `coronaryTree.ts` imports for `samplePos`.
   - S10 depends on S5, S6, S7 and S9.
   - S5 depends on S9 for `coronaryFlow`.
   - S11 depends on S5, S7, S9 and S10 for replay snapshots.
4. **Move "build CoronaryCase from TreeVessel radii and lesions" from S14 (wave 3) into S9 (wave 2).** S5's transport needs per-vessel flow in wave 2. `physiology.flow()` only accepts a `CoronaryCase`.
5. **S10 rewrites `AngioPci.tsx` in wave 2 and removes the PCI step controls, the "Load on the wire" button and the atm slider.** S14 only replaces them in wave 3, so the PCI lab would be unusable between waves.
   - Keep the legacy PCI controls behind the same flag as the legacy `computeTip`.
   - S14's references to `AngioPci.tsx` lines will be stale after S10. `pciDevices` is actually at lines 553-686, not 572-650.
6. **Shared-file edits are written as prose.** Each stream should instead emit unified diffs against the wave-start copy into `patches/<stream>/`, so the integrator can detect conflicts mechanically. This matters most for `useSimulatorStore.ts`, `AngioPci.tsx` and `sceneBuilder.ts`, which take edits from 4-5 streams.

## B. File ownership conflicts and orphaned consumers

7. **ANAT_FS is not data-driven.** `ANAT_COUNT=19` and `CARVE` are compile-time values. ANAT_FS hard-codes `iv[3]`, `iv[6]` and `iv[7..11]` (`XrayRenderer.ts` lines 189-191). S3a's 8-12 fitted heart primitives and S4's great vessels therefore require shader edits in a file S2 owns.
   - Add an S2 slot task: generate ANAT_FS from a tissue-class layout table exported by `thorax.ts`.
   - Move the primitive arrays to a UBO.
8. **S2b's "buildTubes is deleted" breaks ribs, calcium and pulmonary vessels.** All three use `TubeSpec` ribbons, including negative inner shells (`sceneBuilder` lines 215-222 and `thorax.ts` lung ribbons). SEG_FS as written only writes iodine and metal.
   - S2b must write all three accumulation channels and support hollow shells analytically.
   - S4 must own moving ribs and calcium onto segments.
9. **`helpers.ts` (owned by S7) is mostly UI colour helpers.** It is imported by AnatomyScene, CoachPanel, Simulator, CatheterHub and PressureWave. `catheterPath` is imported by `AngioPci.tsx` and `FluoroView.tsx` (both S10). Move `catheterPath` into `src/physics/legacyCatheter.ts` and leave `helpers.ts` with S10.
10. **Existing files in the affected import graph with no owner** (rule: keep exports stable or take ownership):
    - `ViewTrainer.tsx` uses `cameraBasis` and `elongation` → S1.
    - `PressureTrainer.tsx` uses `HEART_PERIOD`.
    - `PhysiologyLab.tsx` uses `physiology.ts`.
    - `McsLab.tsx` and `useCirculation.ts` use `circulation.ts`.
    - `PacingLab.tsx` uses `pacing.ts`.
    - `PericardioLab.tsx` and `BedsideLab.tsx` use `pericardiocentesis.ts`.
    - `PciBench.tsx` uses `pciBench.ts`.
    - `CatheterLab.tsx` uses `catheters.ts` scalars.
    - `store.test.ts` → S10.
11. **More than one heart clock exists.** Besides the 72 bpm default in sceneBuilder there are:
    - `HEART_PERIOD` 0.84 s in `pressure.ts`, used by `FluoroView` line 263, `PressureWave` and `PressureTrainer`;
    - `ECG_BASE_PERIOD` 0.84 s in `ecg.ts`;
    - `HR = 70` in `physiology.ts`.

    S1 or S9 must enumerate and migrate all of them.
12. **Other ownership fixes.**
    - S0 owns `realism.test.ts` but says other streams "flip" its tests. Thresholds should live in `realism_targets.json`, and activation should sit in each stream's own test file.
    - `xrayCapture.ts` must be updated whenever S5 changes `SceneInput`. List this as an S5 shared edit.
    - `XrayRenderer.create()` takes an `HTMLCanvasElement` only, so offscreen capture needs an S2 signature change.

## C. Architecture and budget

13. **Segment count is about 4× the plan's scale.** The current scene has 6,168 tube segments in 874 tubes (2,220 coronary samples in 119 vessels), measured with buildXrayScene in RAO caudal cine.
    - S2b's "1,500 segments ≤1.5 ms binning" is the wrong scale. After S3b growth to 0.4 mm and S4 pulmonary trees, plan for 15-30k segments.
    - Re-budget CPU binning, possibly with a hierarchical per-vessel bounding box.
    - Cache the S3b topology per genome. `AngioPci` rebuilds the tree three times on every lumen change (lines 73-77), so growth must not run inside `buildCoronaryTree` on lesion changes.
14. **SEG_FS's 24-entry local array is smaller than the plan's own occupancy figures.** The audit saw a per-tile maximum of 40-60 segments, and S4 allows p95 ≤32.
    - Specify overflow behaviour and a test for it.
    - Render pulmonary trees and ribs in a separate additive pass, since they need no union with iodine.
    - Consider CPU depth-presorting per tile to cut register pressure on integrated GPUs.
15. **The GPU target is inconsistent.** The renderer is already at 2.4-7.4 ms at 768². The target is ≤8 ms at 1024² (1.78× the pixels) while adding the pyramid, MTF, 3D clutter, segments, histogram and motion-compensated recursion.
    - Measure the current per-pass breakdown first, then allocate a per-pass budget table.
    - The worker budget is 8 ms in the vision but 2 ms in S7 and measurementTargets. Pick one figure per GPU class.
16. **Wrong extension name.** In WebGL2 the extension is `EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2`, not `EXT_disjoint_timer_query`. WebKit does not expose it, so the `gl.finish()` plus CPU timing fallback is mandatory there.
17. **Histogram precision.** Additive blending into float targets needs `EXT_float_blend` for 32F. With 16F, counts above 2048 lose precision, and mip-4 can put up to 4096 points in one bin. Use weights of 1/N or mip-5.
18. **Determinism.** "Byte-identical captures" fails if the one-frame-late PBO/fence histogram is still pending. The capture mode needs synchronous readback and a cleared recursion buffer.
19. **Velocity buffer.**
    - S2b writing velocity means the accumulation pass needs MRT, and the anatomy and bone passes must set `drawBuffers` for it. Specify this in the S2 slot API.
    - Drop "analytic anatomy velocity from heartMotion". It needs a second anatomy evaluation. Use motion-adaptive weights only for anatomy borders.
20. **Avoid double-counting motion.** S3a adds `rootDisplacement` to catheter nodes in `moveWorld`. Once S7 rods run in moving lumens, this counts twice. Restrict the tether to the legacy `catheterPath` fallback.
    - The worker must stamp its node buffers with clock time, and sceneBuilder must evaluate the tree at that same time. Otherwise the tip separates from the ostium by up to about 5 px per frame in systole.
21. **Rewind-and-branch needs a snapshot contract.** Add a `Snapshot` contract to S1 `types.ts` with `serialize` and `restore` and a determinism test, implemented by the S5 transport, S6 dose, the S7 worker, the S9 engine and S15 agents.
22. **Cine storage has no memory budget.** One 50-frame run is about 13 MB at 512² 8-bit and about 52 MB at 1024². Store at 512 or store state and re-render.
23. **Clutter fitting must go through the full chain.** S4's `clutter_stats.py` measures spectra after vendor processing. Putting those spectra straight into the 3D field and then applying S2's harmonisation and edge boost double-applies enhancement. Fit clutter amplitude through the full simulated chain against the targets.
24. **Spectral decomposition crosses streams.** It needs per-material path lengths, but ANAT_FS currently sums everything into one R channel using `MU` in `thorax.ts`, which S4 owns. This is a cross-stream change; schedule it explicitly.
25. **Sample parameterisation.** S3b's septal branches (intramyocardial) and the AV-groove ring behind the root cannot be expressed as `(ell, phi, h)` samples on the current surface. Extend the `Sample` contract in a coordinated S3a/S3b interface task.

## D. Vague or unverifiable acceptance criteria

26. **S1 presets.** I measured `dominance` plus `dominance-main` (1,625 unique runs with angles; families split at |angle| >10°). The plan's "within 2° of the measured median" target is not met as written, and the result depends on how views are classified.

    | View | Measured median | Plan |
    |---|---|---|
    | RCA LAO | LAO 24.7 / CRA -0.7 | LAO 26 |
    | LAO caudal | LAO 25.2 / CAU 26.3 | LAO 26 / CAU 27 |
    | LAO cranial | LAO 20.4 / CRA 21.3 | 22 / 22 |
    | RAO cranial | RAO 25.8 / CRA 22.6 | 27 / 24 |
    | RAO caudal | RAO 17.8 / CAU 14.9 | 24 / 19 |
    | AP cranial | LAO 1.1 / CRA 29.2 | LAO 3 / CRA 29 |

    The plan must fix the classification thresholds and the deduplication in a committed script. Off-grid runs came out at 90.2% (0.5° tolerance), consistent with the plan's 88-89%.
27. **Replace visual-only checks with numeric ones.**
    - S1 "matches cdm-00893-LCA-4" → projected tree extents per view against library extents.
    - S4 "no basket-weave lattice" → peaks in the 2D spectral anisotropy of rib-band regions.
    - S4 hardware "plausible contrast" → depth and FWHM bands taken from library frames that contain sternal wires.
    - S4 habitus "varies realistically" → spread of pre-contrast median grey across library patients.
    - S6 "noisier at the limit" → an SD ratio against AP.
    - S12 "Level 10 Master Assessment" is undefined.
28. **RealOrSimDrill.** It must pass simulated clips through the library's own delivery pipeline: 512 px, `sips` JPEG q72 (the encoder used in `scripts/angio_library/common.py` and `build_cadica.py`), the same frame count, fps and crop. Otherwise compression alone gives the answer away. A 50% result from the developer and user alone is not blinded; specify the number of external readers and trials.
29. **Pipeline scale.** State the 512-equivalent resampling for every metric, since lag-1 correlation and the MTF depend on scale.
    - The 0.16 mm MTF sigma is under 1 px at 768 over 230 mm. Fit the effective blur at library pixel scale instead.
    - Quantify JPEG effects by re-encoding npz frames with `sips` and comparing against the library JPEGs of the same runs. Both exist (427 npz under `datasets/raw` and `datasets/extracted`).
